गन्धद्वारेत्यादिभिर्मन्त्रैः सर्वाधिसिक्तकैः ॥ 13 ॥
4.m: with yellow pigment, white mustard seeds, unbroken rice grains, fruits, and the like, / with the mantras beginning with 'Gandhadvārā' and sprinkling all around,

4.s:
adhivāsya tu tatsthānaṃ pūjayet tatra devatāḥ |
gaṇeśaṃ keśavaṃ śakraṃ brahmāṇaṃ cāpi śaṅkaram || 14 ||
4.d:
अधिवास्य तु तत्स्थानं पूजयेत् तत्र देवताः ।
गणेशं केशवं शक्रं ब्रह्माणं चापि शङ्करम् ॥ 14 ॥
4.m: having consecrated that place, he should worship the deities there: / Gaṇeśa, Keśava, Śakra, Brahmā, and also Śaṅkara.

4.s:
umayā sahitaṃ devaṃ sarvāśca gaṇadevatāḥ |
mātṛśca pūjayet tatra nṛpatiḥ sapurohitaḥ || 15 ||
4.d:
उमया सहितं देवं सर्वाश्च गणदेवताः ।
मातृश्च पूजयेत् तत्र नृपतिः सपुरोहितः ॥ 15 ॥
4.m: Along with the god accompanied by Umā, and all the deities of the retinue, / the king, together with the domestic priest, should worship the Mothers there.

4.s:
maṅgalān kalaśān kṛtvā nānānaivedyasañcayān |
pradadyāt pāyasaṃ svāduphalaṃ modakayāvakau || 16 ||
4.d:
मङ्गलान् कलशान् कृत्वा नानानैवेद्यसञ्चयान् ।
प्रदद्यात् पायसं स्वादुफलं मोदकयावकौ ॥ 16 ॥
4.m: Having arranged auspicious water jars and various collections of offerings, / he should present milk-rice, sweet fruits, sweetmeats, and barley gruel.

4.s:
adhivāsya ca tat sthānaṃ dūrvāsiddhārthakākṣataiḥ |
tatsthānāccāpi bhūtāni sārayenmantramīrayan || 17 ||
4.d:
अधिवास्य च तत् स्थानं दूर्वासिद्धार्थकाक्षतैः ।
तत्स्थानाच्चापि भूतानि सारयेन्मन्त्रमीरयन् ॥ 17 ॥
4.m: And having consecrated that place with dūrvā grass, white mustard seeds, and unbroken grains, / reciting a mantra, he should also expel the spirits from that site.

4.s:
apasarpantu te bhūtā ye bhūtā bhūmipālakāḥ |
hūtānāmavirodhena snānakarma karomyaham || 18 ||
4.d:
अपसर्पन्तु ते भूता ये भूता भूमिपालकाः ।
हूतानामविरोधेन स्नानकर्म करोम्यहम् ॥ 18 ॥
4.m: "May those bhūtas depart who are guardians of the earth; / without hindrance from the spirits, I perform the rite of bathing."

4.s:
tataḥ karau puṭīkṛtya mantreṇānena pārthivaḥ |
āvāhayedimān devān pūjyān puṣyābhiṣekataḥ || 19 ||
4.d:
ततः करौ पुटीकृत्य मन्त्रेणानेन पार्थिवः ।
आवाहयेदिमान् देवान् पूज्यान् पुष्याभिषेकतः ॥ 19 ॥
4.m: Then, folding his hands, the king with this mantra / should invoke these deities who are to be worshipped for the Puṣya coronation:

4.s:
āgacchantu surāḥ sarve ye'tra pūjābhilāṣiṇaḥ |
diśo hi pālakāḥ sarve ye cānye'pyaṃśabhāginaḥ || 20 ||
4.d:
आगच्छन्तु सुराः सर्वे येऽत्र पूजाभिलाषिणः ।
दिशो हि पालकाः सर्वे ये चान्येऽप्यंशभागिनः ॥ 20 ॥
4.m: "May all the gods come who desire worship here, / all the guardians of the quarters, and whoever else has a share!"

4.s:
tataḥ puṣpāñjaliṃ dattvā punarmantraṃ paṭhedimam |
adya tiṣṭhantu vibudhāḥ sthānamāsādya māmakam || 21 ||
4.d:
ततः पुष्पाञ्जलिं दत्त्वा पुनर्मन्त्रं पठेदिमम् ।
अद्य तिष्ठन्तु विबुधाः स्थानमासाद्य मामकम् ॥ 21 ॥
4.m: Then, offering a handful of flowers, he should recite this mantra again: / "May the gods stay today, having arrived at my dwelling,

4.s:
svapūjāṃ prāpya pātāro dattvā śāntiṃ mahībhuje |
tatastāṃ nṛpatī rātriṃ nayet tu sapurohitaḥ || 22 ||
4.d:
स्वपूजां प्राप्य पातारो दत्त्वा शान्तिं महीभुजे ।
ततस्तां नृपती रात्रिं नयेत् तु सपुरोहितः ॥ 22 ॥
4.m: receiving their own worship, the protectors granting peace to the king!" / Then the king should spend that night together with his royal priest.

4.s:
svapne śubhāśubhaṃ vidyānnṛpastu sapurohitaḥ |
kṛtvā pūjāṃ tu devānāṃ rātrau sthāne nṛpaḥ svapet || 23 ||
4.d:
स्वप्ने शुभाशुभं विद्यान्नृपस्तु सपुरोहितः ।
कृत्वा पूजां तु देवानां रात्रौ स्थाने नृपः स्वपेत् ॥ 23 ॥
4.m: In a dream the king, accompanied by his royal priest, should perceive the auspicious and inauspicious. / Having performed worship of the gods, the king should sleep in that place at night.

4.s:
śubhāśubhaphalaṃ svapne jñeyaṃ oṣajñasammate |
duḥsvapnadarśanaṃ cet syāt tadā puṣyābhiṣecane || 24 ||
4.d:
शुभाशुभफलं स्वप्ने ज्ञेयं ओषज्ञसम्मते ।
दुःस्वप्नदर्शनं चेत् स्यात् तदा पुष्याभिषेचने ॥ 24 ॥
4.m: The auspicious or inauspicious fruit should be known in a dream according to the approval of dream-experts. / If there should be the seeing of a bad dream, then during the Puṣya coronation

4.s:
homaṃ caturguṇaṃ kuryād dattvā cāpi gavāṃ śatam |
govājikuṃjarāṇāṃ tu prāsādasya girestatroḥ || 25 ||
4.d:
होमं चतुर्गुणं कुर्याद् दत्त्वा चापि गवां शतम् ।
गोवाजिकुंजराणां तु प्रासादस्य गिरेस्तत्रोः ॥ 25 ॥
4.m: he should perform fourfold oblation and also give a hundred cows. / Ascending cattle, horses, and elephants, a palace, a mountain, or a tree

4.s:
ārohaṇaṃ śubhakar'm rājyaśrīvṛddhikārakam |
dadhidevasuvarṇānāṃ rāhmaṇasya pradarśanam || 26 ||
4.d:
आरोहणं शुभकर्ऽम् राज्यश्रीवृद्धिकारकम् ।
दधिदेवसुवर्णानां राह्मणस्य प्रदर्शनम् ॥ 26 ॥
4.m: brings good fortune and causes increase of royal sovereignty. / The seeing of curds, a deity, gold, or a brāhmaṇa,

4.s:
vīṇādūrvākṣataphalaṃ puṣpacchatravilepanam |
śītāṃśu akraśaṃkhānāṃ padmasya suhṛdastathā || 27 ||
4.d:
वीणादूर्वाक्षतफलं पुष्पच्छत्रविलेपनम् ।
शीतांशु अक्रशंखानां पद्मस्य सुहृदस्तथा ॥ 27 ॥
4.m: a lute, dūrvā grass, unbroken grain, fruit, flowers, an umbrella, anointing paste, / the moon, Indra, conches, a lotus, and likewise a friend,

4.s:
lābhāḥ kṣayakarāḥ śatrau ratnākarasya bhūbhṛtaḥ |
darśanaṃ coparāgasya nigaḍena ca bandhanam || 28 ||
4.d:
लाभाः क्षयकराः शत्रौ रत्नाकरस्य भूभृतः ।
दर्शनं चोपरागस्य निगडेन च बन्धनम् ॥ 28 ॥
4.m: bring gain and ruin to the enemy. For a king, / the seeing of an ocean, of an eclipse, and binding with chains,

4.s:
māṃsasya bhojanaṃ caiva parvatasya vivartanam |
ābhimadhye tarūtpattirmṛtaṃ pratyanurodanam || 29 ||
4.d:
मांसस्य भोजनं चैव पर्वतस्य विवर्तनम् ।
आभिमध्ये तरूत्पत्तिर्मृतं प्रत्यनुरोदनम् ॥ 29 ॥
4.m: eating meat, turning around on a mountain, / a tree growing inside the navel, weeping over a dead person,

4.s:
agamyāgamanaṃ kūpa paṅkagarbhāvatīrṇatā |
parvatasya tathā nadyāḥ rotasāṃ laṅghanaṃ tathā || 30 ||
4.d:
अगम्यागमनं कूप पङ्कगर्भावतीर्णता ।
पर्वतस्य तथा नद्याः रोतसां लङ्घनं तथा ॥ 30 ॥
4.m: approaching a woman not to be approached, descending into the depths of a well or mud, / and crossing a mountain, a river, or streams,

4.s:
svaputramaraṇaṃ caiva pānaṃ rudhiramadyayoḥ |
bhojanaṃ pāyasasyāpi manuṣyārohaṇaṃ tathā || 31 ||
4.d:
स्वपुत्रमरणं चैव पानं रुधिरमद्ययोः ।
भोजनं पायसस्यापि मनुष्यारोहणं तथा ॥ 31 ॥
4.m: the death of one's own son, drinking blood and liquor, / eating milk-rice, and riding upon a human being—

4.s:
kalyāṇasukhasaubhāgya-rājya-śatrukṣayaṃ tathā |
ete svapnāḥ prakurvanti nṛpasya nṛpasattama || 32 ||
4.d:
कल्याणसुखसौभाग्य-राज्य-शत्रुक्षयं तथा ।
एते स्वप्नाः प्रकुर्वन्ति नृपस्य नृपसत्तम ॥ 32 ॥
4.m: these dreams produce welfare, happiness, good fortune, / sovereignty, and the destruction of enemies for a king, O best of kings!

4.s:
kharoṣṭramahiṣāṇāṃ ca āroho rājyanāśanaḥ |
nṛtyaṃ gītaṃ tathā hāsyaṃ pāṭhaścāpyaśubhapradaḥ || 33 ||
4.d:
खरोष्ट्रमहिषाणां च आरोहो राज्यनाशनः ।
नृत्यं गीतं तथा हास्यं पाठश्चाप्यशुभप्रदः ॥ 33 ॥
4.m: Riding donkeys, camels, and buffaloes destroys one's kingdom; / dancing, singing, laughing, and recitation also bring ill fortune.

4.s:
raktavastraparidhānaṃ raktamālānulepanam |
raktāṃ kṛṣṇāṃ striyaṃ caiva kāmayan mṛtyumāpnuyāt || 34 ||
4.d:
रक्तवस्त्रपरिधानं रक्तमालानुलेपनम् ।
रक्तां कृष्णां स्त्रियं चैव कामयन् मृत्युमाप्नुयात् ॥ 34 ॥
4.m: Wearing red garments, wearing red garlands and paste, / and desiring a red or black woman brings about death.

4.s:
kūpāntare praveśaḥ syād dakṣiṇāśāgatistathā |
paṅke nimajjanaṃ snānaṃ bhāryāputravināśanam || 35 ||
4.d:
कूपान्तरे प्रवेशः स्याद् दक्षिणाशागतिस्तथा ।
पङ्के निमज्जनं स्नानं भार्यापुत्रविनाशनम् ॥ 35 ॥
4.m: Entering inside a well, going in the southern direction, / sinking in mud, bathing, and the destruction of wife and son—

4.s:
lābhastasya bhavet svapneapyarutpattirnṛpabhya ca |
ādāya garbhanāḍīṃ tu sakuno yātihañjanaḥ || 36 ||
4.d:
लाभस्तस्य भवेत् स्वप्नेअप्यरुत्पत्तिर्नृपभ्य च ।
आदाय गर्भनाडीं तु सकुनो यातिहञ्जनः ॥ 36 ॥
4.m: the gain of these in a dream and the sprouting of […] for a king, / [or if] a bird, a wagtail, goes taking the umbilical cord,

4.s:
sa tu rājyāntaraṃ prāpya mahākalyāṇamāpnuyāt |
dīrghaṃ viṃśatihastaṃ tu hastaṣoḍaśavistṛtam || 37 ||
4.d:
स तु राज्यान्तरं प्राप्य महाकल्याणमाप्नुयात् ।
दीर्घं विंशतिहस्तं तु हस्तषोडशविस्तृतम् ॥ 37 ॥
4.m: he, having obtained another kingdom, will attain great prosperity. / Twenty cubits long and sixteen cubits wide,

4.s:
kuryāt tu lakṣaṇopetaṃ yajñamaṇḍalamuttamam |
tato'pare'hni pūrvāhṇe mātṛṇāṃ pūjanaṃ caret || 38 ||
4.d:
कुर्यात् तु लक्षणोपेतं यज्ञमण्डलमुत्तमम् ।
ततोऽपरेऽह्नि पूर्वाह्णे मातृणां पूजनं चरेत् ॥ 38 ॥
4.m: he should make an excellent sacrificial pavilion endowed with the proper characteristics. / Then on the next day, in the forenoon, he should perform the worship of the Mothers,

4.s:
kuḍyalagnāṃ vasordhārāṃ vṛddhiśrāddhaṃ tathaiva ca |
candanāgurukastūrīdhūmakarpūracūrṇakaiḥ || 39 ||
4.d:
कुड्यलग्नां वसोर्धारां वृद्धिश्राद्धं तथैव च ।
चन्दनागुरुकस्तूरीधूमकर्पूरचूर्णकैः ॥ 39 ॥
4.m: the stream of wealth trickling down the wall, and likewise the vṛddhi-śrāddha. / With powders of sandalwood, agallochum, musk, incense, and camphor,

4.s:
sampūjya maṇḍalasthānaṃ tasmin hrauṃ śambhave namaḥ |
astrāya huṃ phaḍityevaṃ likhenmantradvayaṃ budhaḥ || 40 ||
4.d:
सम्पूज्य मण्डलस्थानं तस्मिन् ह्रौं शम्भवे नमः ।
अस्त्राय हुं फडित्येवं लिखेन्मन्त्रद्वयं बुधः ॥ 40 ॥
4.m: having worshipped the site of the maṇḍala, upon it the wise one should draw / these two mantras: "hrauṃ, homage to Śambhu" and "To the weapon: huṃ phaṭ!"

4.s:
mantravinmaṇḍalajñaśca sūtraiḥ kambalasambhavaiḥ |
kauśeyairvā svastikākhyaṃ prathamaṃ maṇḍalaṃ likhet || 41 ||
4.d:
मन्त्रविन्मण्डलज्ञश्च सूत्रैः कम्बलसम्भवैः ।
कौशेयैर्वा स्वस्तिकाख्यं प्रथमं मण्डलं लिखेत् ॥ 41 ॥
4.m: The knower of mantras and knower of maṇḍalas, with cords made of wool / or with silk ones, should first draw the maṇḍala named svastika.

4.s:
caturhastapramāṇaṃ tu maṇḍalaṃ vilikhet tataḥ |
hastapramāṇaṃ padmaṃ tu maṇḍalasya prakīrtitam || 42 ||
4.d:
चतुर्हस्तप्रमाणं तु मण्डलं विलिखेत् ततः ।
हस्तप्रमाणं पद्मं तु मण्डलस्य प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 42 ॥
4.m: He should then draw the maṇḍala four cubits in measure; / the lotus of the maṇḍala is declared to be one cubit in measure,

4.s:
dvārāṇi sārdhahastāni karṇikākeśarojjvalam |
sitaṃ raktaṃ ca pītaṃ ca kṛṣṇaṃ haritameva ca || 43 ||
4.d:
द्वाराणि सार्धहस्तानि कर्णिकाकेशरोज्ज्वलम् ।
सितं रक्तं च पीतं च कृष्णं हरितमेव च ॥ 43 ॥
4.m: the gates one and a half cubits, bright with pericarp and filaments. / White, red, yellow, black, and green:

4.s:
śālicūrṇaiśca kausumbhairhāridrairharidudbhavaiḥ |
kuryāt tathāñjanaiścūrṇai rājā maṇḍalavṛddhaye || 44 ||
4.d:
शालिचूर्णैश्च कौसुम्भैर्हारिद्रैर्हरिदुद्भवैः ।
कुर्यात् तथाञ्जनैश्चूर्णै राजा मण्डलवृद्धये ॥ 44 ॥
4.m: with rice flour, safflower, turmeric, and powders derived from green [plants], / as well as collyrium powders, the king should make [it] for the augmentation of the maṇḍala.

4.s:
padmāntataḥ samāabhya tālaṃ paścimagāminam |
paścimadvāramadhye ca satapatraṃ vinirdiśet || 45 ||
4.d:
पद्मान्ततः समाअभ्य तालं पश्चिमगामिनम् ।
पश्चिमद्वारमध्ये च सतपत्रं विनिर्दिशेत् ॥ 45 ॥
4.m: Beginning from the edge of the lotus, going westward by a span, / in the middle of the western gate he should prescribe a hundred-petalled [lotus].

4.s:
pratyekaṃ dvāramadhye tu padmaṃ caivāṣṭapatrakam |
kuryānmaṇḍalabhāgajñaścūrṇaireva pṛthak pṛthak || 46 ||
4.d:
प्रत्येकं द्वारमध्ये तु पद्मं चैवाष्टपत्रकम् ।
कुर्यान्मण्डलभागज्ञश्चूर्णैरेव पृथक् पृथक् ॥ 46 ॥
4.m: In the middle of each gate, an eight-petalled lotus / the expert in the divisions of the maṇḍala should make with those separate powders.

4.s:
cūrṇaistu maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā sūtrāṇyutsārayet tataḥ |
utsārya sūtraṃ prathamaṃ maṇḍalaṃ pūjayet tataḥ || 47 ||
4.d:
चूर्णैस्तु मण्डलं कृत्वा सूत्राण्युत्सारयेत् ततः ।
उत्सार्य सूत्रं प्रथमं मण्डलं पूजयेत् ततः ॥ 47 ॥
4.m: Having made the maṇḍala with the powders, he should then remove the cords; / having first removed the cord, he should then worship the maṇḍala.

4.s:
havanāya nama iti tato hastaṃ viyojayet |
savyāvalambahastaṃ tu rajaḥpātraṃ samācaret || 48 ||
4.d:
हवनाय नम इति ततो हस्तं वियोजयेत् ।
सव्यावलम्बहस्तं तु रजःपात्रं समाचरेत् ॥ 48 ॥
4.m: With "Homage to the offering!" he should then apply his hand; / keeping his left hand supporting it, he should manipulate the powder-vessel.

4.s:
madhyamānāmikāṅguṣṭhairupariṣṭād yathecchayā |
adhomukhāṅgulīḥ kṛtvā pātayecca vicakṣaṇaḥ || 49 ||
4.d:
मध्यमानामिकाङ्गुष्ठैरुपरिष्टाद् यथेच्छया ।
अधोमुखाङ्गुलीः कृत्वा पातयेच्च विचक्षणः ॥ 49 ॥
4.m: With the middle finger, ring finger, and thumb, from above as desired, / having turned his fingers downward, the wise man should let [the powder] fall.

4.s:
samārekhā tu kartavyā vicchitrā puṣparañjitā |
aṅguṣṭhaparvanaipuṇyāt samā kāryā vijānatā || 50 ||
4.d:
समारेखा तु कर्तव्या विच्छित्रा पुष्परञ्जिता ।
अङ्गुष्ठपर्वनैपुण्यात् समा कार्या विजानता ॥ 50 ॥
4.m: An even line should be made, variegated and colored like flowers; / through skill with the joint of the thumb, an even line must be made by one who knows.

4.s:
saṃsaktaviṣamaṃ sthūlaṃ vicchinnaṃ kṛsarakṛtim |
paryantamarpitaṃ hrasvamālikhenna kadācana || 51 ||
4.d:
संसक्तविषमं स्थूलं विच्छिन्नं कृसरकृतिम् ।
पर्यन्तमर्पितं ह्रस्वमालिखेन्न कदाचन ॥ 51 ॥
4.m: Overlapping, uneven, too thick, broken, resembling kṛsara, / extended to the edge, or too short—one should never draw such.

4.s:
saṃsakte kalahaṃ vidyādūrdhva rekhe tu vigraham |
atisthūle bhaved vyādhirnityaṃ pīḍāvimiśrite || 52 ||
4.d:
संसक्ते कलहं विद्यादूर्ध्व रेखे तु विग्रहम् ।
अतिस्थूले भवेद् व्याधिर्नित्यं पीडाविमिश्रिते ॥ 52 ॥
4.m: In overlapping [lines] one should know quarrel, in an upward line conflict, / in one too thick there will be disease, and in a mixed one constant suffering.

4.s:
bindubhirbhayamāpnoti śatrupakṣānna saṃśayaḥ |
kṛśāyāṃ cārthahāni syācchinnāyāṃ maraṇaṃ dhruvam || 53 ||
4.d:
बिन्दुभिर्भयमाप्नोति शत्रुपक्षान्न संशयः ।
कृशायां चार्थहानि स्याच्छिन्नायां मरणं ध्रुवम् ॥ 53 ॥
4.m: From drops one incurs fear from the enemy's faction, without a doubt; / in a thin [line] there is loss of wealth, and in a broken one, certain death,

4.s:
viyogo vā bhavet tasya iṣṭadravyasutasya vā |
aviditvā likhed yastu maṇḍalaṃ tu yathecchayā || 54 ||
4.d:
वियोगो वा भवेत् तस्य इष्टद्रव्यसुतस्य वा ।
अविदित्वा लिखेद् यस्तु मण्डलं तु यथेच्छया ॥ 54 ॥
4.m: or there would be separation from a desired object or son. / But he who, without knowing, draws a maṇḍala according to his whim

4.s:
sarvadoṣānavāpnoti ye doṣāḥ ūrvamīritāḥ |
sitasarṣapadūrvāyā rekhāḥ kāryā vijānatā || 55 ||
4.d:
सर्वदोषानवाप्नोति ये दोषाः ऊर्वमीरिताः ।
सितसर्षपदूर्वाया रेखाः कार्या विजानता ॥ 55 ॥
4.m: incurs all the faults that were spoken of before. / The lines are to be made with white mustard and dūrvā grass by one who knows.

4.s:
vimalaṃ vijayaṃ bhadraṃ vimānaṃ śubhadaṃ śivam |
vardhamānaṃ ca devaṃ ca śatākṣaṃ kāmadāyakam || 56 ||
4.d:
विमलं विजयं भद्रं विमानं शुभदं शिवम् ।
वर्धमानं च देवं च शताक्षं कामदायकम् ॥ 56 ॥
4.m: Vimala, Vijaya, Bhadra, Vimāna, Śubhada, Śiva, / Vardhamāna, Deva, Śatākṣa, Kāmadāyaka,

4.s:
rucikaṃ svastikaṃ caiva dvādaśaite tu maṇḍalāḥ |
yathāsthānaṃ yathāyajñaṃ yojanīyā vicakṣaṇaiḥ || 57 ||
4.d:
रुचिकं स्वस्तिकं चैव द्वादशैते तु मण्डलाः ।
यथास्थानं यथायज्ञं योजनीया विचक्षणैः ॥ 57 ॥
4.m: Rucika, and Svastika—these are the twelve maṇḍalas; / according to place and sacrifice, they are to be employed by the wise.

4.s:
sāgare madhyamāne tu pīyūṣārthaṃ surotkaraiḥ |
pīyūṣadhāraṇārthāya nirmitā viśvakarmaṇā || 58 ||
4.d:
सागरे मध्यमाने तु पीयूषार्थं सुरोत्करैः ।
पीयूषधारणार्थाय निर्मिता विश्वकर्मणा ॥ 58 ॥
4.m: When the ocean was being churned for nectar by the hosts of gods, / for the sake of holding the nectar, [jars] were fashioned by Viśvakarman.

4.s:
kalāṃ kalāṃ tu devānāmasitvā te pṛthak pṛthak |
yataḥ kṛtāstu kalasāstataste parikīrtitāḥ || 59 ||
4.d:
कलां कलां तु देवानामसित्वा ते पृथक् पृथक् ।
यतः कृतास्तु कलसास्ततस्ते परिकीर्तिताः ॥ 59 ॥
4.m: Drawing a portion from each of the gods separately, / because they were made as portions, they are proclaimed as jars.

4.s:
navaiva kalasāḥ proktā nāmatastānnibodhata |
gohyopagohyo maruto mayūkhaśca tathāparaḥ || 60 ||
4.d:
नवैव कलसाः प्रोक्ता नामतस्तान्निबोधत ।
गोह्योपगोह्यो मरुतो मयूखश्च तथापरः ॥ 60 ॥
4.m: Nine jars indeed are declared; learn them by name: / Gohya, Upagohya, Marut, and another is Mayūkha,

4.s:
manohācāryabhadraśca vijayastanu dūṣakaḥ |
indriyaghno'tha vijayo navamaḥ parikīrtitaḥ || 61 ||
4.d:
मनोहाचार्यभद्रश्च विजयस्तनु दूषकः ।
इन्द्रियघ्नोऽथ विजयो नवमः परिकीर्तितः ॥ 61 ॥
4.m: Manoha, Ācārya, Bhadra, Vijaya, Tanudūṣaka, / Indriyaghna, and Vijaya is proclaimed as the ninth.

4.s:
teṣāmeva kramād bhūpa nava nāmāni yāni tu |
śṛṇu tānyaparāṇyeva śāntidāni sadaiva hi || 62 ||
4.d:
तेषामेव क्रमाद् भूप नव नामानि यानि तु ।
शृणु तान्यपराण्येव शान्तिदानि सदैव हि ॥ 62 ॥
4.m: Hear now, O king, their other nine names in due order, / which indeed always bestow peace:

4.s:
kṣitīndraḥ prathamaḥ prokto dvitīyo jalasambhavaḥ |
pavanāgnī tato dve tu yajamanastataḥ paraḥ || 63 ||
4.d:
क्षितीन्द्रः प्रथमः प्रोक्तो द्वितीयो जलसम्भवः ।
पवनाग्नी ततो द्वे तु यजमनस्ततः परः ॥ 63 ॥
4.m: The first is called Kṣitīndra, the second is Jalasambhava, / then two are Pavana and Agni, and after that is Yajamāna;

4.s:
koṣasambhavāmnā tu ṣaṣṭhaḥ sa parikīrtitaḥ |
somastu saptamaḥ prokta ādityastu tathāṣṭamaḥ || 64 ||
4.d:
कोषसम्भवाम्ना तु षष्ठः स परिकीर्तितः ।
सोमस्तु सप्तमः प्रोक्त आदित्यस्तु तथाष्टमः ॥ 64 ॥
4.m: the sixth is celebrated by the name Koṣasambhava, / the seventh is called Soma, and likewise the eighth is Āditya;

4.s:
vijayo nāma kalaso yo'sau navama ucyate |
sa tu paṃcamukhaḥ prokto mahādevasvarūpadhṛk || 65 ||
4.d:
विजयो नाम कलसो योऽसौ नवम उच्यते ।
स तु पंचमुखः प्रोक्तो महादेवस्वरूपधृक् ॥ 65 ॥
4.m: and the jar named Vijaya, which is designated the ninth, / is said to be five-mouthed, assuming the form of Mahādeva.

4.s:
ghaṭasya pañcavaktreṣu pañcavaktraḥ svayaṃ tathā |
yathākāṣṭhāṃ sthitaḥ samyag vāmadevādināmataḥ || 66 ||
4.d:
घटस्य पञ्चवक्त्रेषु पञ्चवक्त्रः स्वयं तथा ।
यथाकाष्ठां स्थितः सम्यग् वामदेवादिनामतः ॥ 66 ॥
4.m: On the five mouths of the pot, the five-mouthed one [Śiva] himself is thus / properly positioned according to the quarters, under the names Vāmadeva and the rest.

4.s:
maṇḍalasya tu padmānte pañcavaktraṃ ghaṭaṃ nyaset |
kṣitīndraṃ pūrvato nyasya paścime jalasambhavam || 67 ||
4.d:
मण्डलस्य तु पद्मान्ते पञ्चवक्त्रं घटं न्यसेत् ।
क्षितीन्द्रं पूर्वतो न्यस्य पश्चिमे जलसम्भवम् ॥ 67 ॥
4.m: At the lotus-tip of the maṇḍala one should place the five-mouthed pot; / having placed Kṣitīndra in the east, and Jalasambhava in the west,

4.s:
vāyavye vāyavaṃ nyasya āgneye hyagnisambhavam |
nair-ṛtye yajamānaṃ tu aiśānyāṃ koṣasambhavam || 68 ||
4.d:
वायव्ये वायवं न्यस्य आग्नेये ह्यग्निसम्भवम् ।
नैर्-ऋत्ये यजमानं तु ऐशान्यां कोषसम्भवम् ॥ 68 ॥
4.m: having placed Vāyava in the northwest and Agnisambhava in the southeast, / Yajamāna in the southwest, and Koṣasambhava in the northeast,

4.s:
somamuttarato yojyaṃ sauraṃ dakṣiṇato nyaset |
nyasyaivaṃ kalasāṃścaiva teṣu caitān vicintayet || 69 ||
4.d:
सोममुत्तरतो योज्यं सौरं दक्षिणतो न्यसेत् ।
न्यस्यैवं कलसांश्चैव तेषु चैतान् विचिन्तयेत् ॥ 69 ॥
4.m: one should join Soma in the north and place Saura in the south. / Having thus arranged the jars, one should contemplate these [deities] within them:

4.s:
kalasānāṃ mukhe brahmā grīvāyāṃ śaṅkaraḥ sthitaḥ |
mūle tu saṃsthito viṣṇurmadhye mātṛgaṇāḥ sthitāḥ || 70 ||
4.d:
कलसानां मुखे ब्रह्मा ग्रीवायां शङ्करः स्थितः ।
मूले तु संस्थितो विष्णुर्मध्ये मातृगणाः स्थिताः ॥ 70 ॥
4.m: Brahmā resides at the mouth of the jars, Śaṅkara at the neck, / Viṣṇu resides at the base, and the host of Mothers resides in the middle;

4.s:
dikpālā devatāḥ sarvā veṣṭayanti diśo daśa |
kukṣau tu sāgarāḥ sapta saptadvīpāśca saṃsthitāḥ || 71 ||
4.d:
दिक्पाला देवताः सर्वा वेष्टयन्ति दिशो दश ।
कुक्षौ तु सागराः सप्त सप्तद्वीपाश्च संस्थिताः ॥ 71 ॥
4.m: all the gods who are regents of the quarters encompass the ten directions; / in the belly reside the seven oceans and the seven continents;

4.s:
nakṣatrāṇi grahāḥ sarve tathaiva kulaparvatāḥ |
gaṅgādyāḥ saritaḥ sarvā vedāścatvāra eva ca || 72 ||
4.d:
नक्षत्राणि ग्रहाः सर्वे तथैव कुलपर्वताः ।
गङ्गाद्याः सरितः सर्वा वेदाश्चत्वार एव च ॥ 72 ॥
4.m: all the lunar mansions and planets, and likewise the mountain ranges, / all the rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā, and indeed the four Vedas—

4.s:
kalase saṃsthitāḥ sarve teṣu tāni vicintayet |
atnāni sarvabījāni puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca || 73 ||
4.d:
कलसे संस्थिताः सर्वे तेषु तानि विचिन्तयेत् ।
अत्नानि सर्वबीजानि पुष्पाणि च फलानि च ॥ 73 ॥
4.m: all abide in the jar; one should contemplate them within them. / [One should place in them] jewels, all seeds, flowers, and fruits:

4.s:
vajramauktikavaidūryamahāpadmendrasphāṭikaiḥ |
sarvadhāmamayaṃ bilvaṃ nāgarodumbara tathā || 74 ||
4.d:
वज्रमौक्तिकवैदूर्यमहापद्मेन्द्रस्फाटिकैः ।
सर्वधाममयं बिल्वं नागरोदुम्बर तथा ॥ 74 ॥
4.m: with diamond, pearl, cat's-eye, emerald, and crystal; / bilva possessing all splendour, and likewise nāgara and udumbara;

4.s:
bījapūrakajambīrakāśmīrāmrātadāḍimam |
yavaṃ śāliṃ ca nīvāraṃ godhūmaṃ sitasarṣapam || 75 ||
4.d:
बीजपूरकजम्बीरकाश्मीराम्रातदाडिमम् ।
यवं शालिं च नीवारं गोधूमं सितसर्षपम् ॥ 75 ॥
4.m: citron, lime, kāśmīra, mango, hog-plum, and pomegranate; / barley, śāli rice, wild rice, wheat, and white mustard;

4.s:
kuṅkumāgurukarpūramadanaṃ rocanaṃ tathā |
candanaṃ ca tathā māṃsīmelāṃ kuṣṭhaṃ tathaiva ca || 76 ||
4.d:
कुङ्कुमागुरुकर्पूरमदनं रोचनं तथा ।
चन्दनं च तथा मांसीमेलां कुष्ठं तथैव च ॥ 76 ॥
4.m: saffron, aguru, camphor, madana, and rocanā; / sandalwood, and likewise spikenard, cardamom, and costus;

4.s:
astūrīpatracūrṇaṃ ca jalaniryāsakāmbudam |
śaileyaṃ badaraṃ jātīpatrapuṣpe tathaiva ca || 77 ||
4.d:
अस्तूरीपत्रचूर्णं च जलनिर्यासकाम्बुदम् ।
शैलेयं बदरं जातीपत्रपुष्पे तथैव च ॥ 77 ॥
4.m: musk, powder of tejapatra, and bdellium, and mustā; / lichen, jujube, and likewise nut-meg leaf and flower;

4.s:
kālaśākaṃ tathā pṛkkā devīparṇakameva ca |
vacāṃ dhātrīṃ samañjiṣṭhāṃ turuṣkaṃ maṅgalāṣṭakam || 78 ||
4.d:
कालशाकं तथा पृक्का देवीपर्णकमेव च ।
वचां धात्रीं समञ्जिष्ठां तुरुष्कं मङ्गलाष्टकम् ॥ 78 ॥
4.m: kālaśāka, and pṛkkā, and devīparṇaka; / sweet flag, emblic myrobalan, madder, turuṣka, the eight auspicious items;

4.s:
dūrvāṃ mohanikāṃ bhadrāṃ śatamūlīṃ śatāvarīm |
arṇānāṃ saralāṃ kṣudrāṃ sahadevīṃ gajāhvayām || 79 ||
4.d:
दूर्वां मोहनिकां भद्रां शतमूलीं शतावरीम् ।
अर्णानां सरलां क्षुद्रां सहदेवीं गजाह्वयाम् ॥ 79 ॥
4.m: dūrvā grass, mohanikā, bhadrā, śatamūlī, śatāvarī; / arṇānā, saralā, kṣudrā, sahadevī, gajāhvayā;

4.s:
pūrṇakoṣāṃ sitāṃ pīṭhāṃ guñjāṃ śirasikānalau |
vyāmakaṃ gajadantaṃ ca śatapuṣpaṃ punarnabām || 80 ||
4.d:
पूर्णकोषां सितां पीठां गुञ्जां शिरसिकानलौ ।
व्यामकं गजदन्तं च शतपुष्पं पुनर्नबाम् ॥ 80 ॥
4.m: pūrṇakoṣā, sitā, pīṭhā, guñjā, śirasikā, anala; / vyāmaka, and ivory, dill, and punarnavā;

4.s:
brāhmīṃ devīṃ śivāṃ rudrāṃ sarvasandhānikāṃ tathā |
samāhṛtya śubhānetān kalaseṣu nidhārpayet || 81 ||
4.d:
ब्राह्मीं देवीं शिवां रुद्रां सर्वसन्धानिकां तथा ।
समाहृत्य शुभानेतान् कलसेषु निधार्पयेत् ॥ 81 ॥
4.m: brāhmī, devī, śivā, rudrā, and likewise sarvasandhānikā— / having gathered these auspicious items, one should deposit them in the jars.

4.s:
kalasasya yathādeśaṃ vidhiṃ śambhuṃ gadādharam |
yathākramaṃ pūjayitvā śambhu mukhyatayā yajet || 82 ||
4.d:
कलसस्य यथादेशं विधिं शम्भुं गदाधरम् ।
यथाक्रमं पूजयित्वा शम्भु मुख्यतया यजेत् ॥ 82 ॥
4.m: Having worshipped according to their location in the jar, in due order, / Vidhi, Śambhu, and Gadādhara, one should worship Śambhu pre-eminently.

4.s:
prāsādena tu mantreṇa śambhuṃ tantreṇa śaṅkaram |
prathamaṃ pūjayenmadhye nānā naivedyavedanaiḥ || 83 ||
4.d:
प्रासादेन तु मन्त्रेण शम्भुं तन्त्रेण शङ्करम् ।
प्रथमं पूजयेन्मध्ये नाना नैवेद्यवेदनैः ॥ 83 ॥
4.m: With the prāsāda mantra and with the tantra for Śambhu, / one should first worship Śaṅkara in the centre with offerings of various cooked foods.

4.s:
dikpālānāṃ ghaṭeṣveva dikpālānapi pūjayet |
pūrvaṃ bahiḥ sthāpiteṣu grahāṇāṃ kalaseṣu ca || 84 ||
4.d:
दिक्पालानां घटेष्वेव दिक्पालानपि पूजयेत् ।
पूर्वं बहिः स्थापितेषु ग्रहाणां कलसेषु च ॥ 84 ॥
4.m: One should worship the regents of the quarters in the pots of the regents of the quarters, / and in the jars of the planets previously stationed outside,

4.s:
navagrahān pūjayet tu mātṛrmātṛghaṭeṣu ca |
sarve devā ghaṭe pūjyā ghaṭāsteṣāṃ pṛthak pṛthak || 85 ||
4.d:
नवग्रहान् पूजयेत् तु मातृर्मातृघटेषु च ।
सर्वे देवा घटे पूज्या घटास्तेषां पृथक् पृथक् ॥ 85 ॥
4.m: one should worship the nine planets, and the Mothers in the pots of the Mothers; / all gods are to be worshipped in a pot, their pots being separate.

4.s:
navaiva tatra pūrvoktāḥ smṛtā mukhyatayā nṛpa |
bhakṣyairbhojyaiśca peyaiśca puṣpairnānāvidhaiḥ phalaiḥ || 86 ||
4.d:
नवैव तत्र पूर्वोक्ताः स्मृता मुख्यतया नृप ।
भक्ष्यैर्भोज्यैश्च पेयैश्च पुष्पैर्नानाविधैः फलैः ॥ 86 ॥
4.m: Only nine have been mentioned there as principal, O king. / With chewable foods, eatables, beverages, flowers, and various kinds of fruits,

4.s:
yāvakaiḥ pāyasaiścaiva yathāsambhavayojitaiḥ |
puṣyasnānāya nṛpatiḥ pūjayet sakalān surān || 87 ||
4.d:
यावकैः पायसैश्चैव यथासम्भवयोजितैः ।
पुष्यस्नानाय नृपतिः पूजयेत् सकलान् सुरान् ॥ 87 ॥
4.m: with barley preparations and milk-rice properly combined as available, / the king should worship all the gods for the bath on Puṣya.

4.s:
dakṣiṇe maṇḍalasyātha kuṇḍaṃ nirmāya pāyasaiḥ |
samidbhiḥ śālisiddhārthairghṛtairdūrvākṣataistathā || 88 ||
4.d:
दक्षिणे मण्डलस्याथ कुण्डं निर्माय पायसैः ।
समिद्भिः शालिसिद्धार्थैर्घृतैर्दूर्वाक्षतैस्तथा ॥ 88 ॥
4.m: Then, having constructed a fire-pit to the south of the maṇḍala, with milk-rice, / firewood sticks, śāli rice, white mustard, ghee, dūrvā grass, and unbroken grains,

4.s:
kevalaiśca tathaivājyaiḥ pūjitān sakalān surān |
homena toṣayed vṛddhyai nṛpaḥ satvikpurohitaḥ || 89 ||
4.d:
केवलैश्च तथैवाज्यैः पूजितान् सकलान् सुरान् ।
होमेन तोषयेद् वृद्ध्यै नृपः सत्विक्पुरोहितः ॥ 89 ॥
4.m: and likewise with pure ghee, the king, together with the officiating priest and purohita, / should satisfy all the worshipped gods through fire-sacrifice for prosperity.

4.s:
homānte maṇḍalodīcyāṃ vedikāyāṃ sapaṭṭakam |
rocanākhyamalaṃkārāṃstathā sarvān niyojayet || 90 ||
4.d:
होमान्ते मण्डलोदीच्यां वेदिकायां सपट्टकम् ।
रोचनाख्यमलंकारांस्तथा सर्वान् नियोजयेत् ॥ 90 ॥
4.m: At the conclusion of the fire-sacrifice, on a platform to the north of the maṇḍala, / he should set out [the board] with silk cloth, rocanā, and all ornaments.

4.s:
vṛddhāvaṅgulamaṅgulyā ṣaḍviṃśāṅgulikāvadhi |
vṛttaṃ vā caturasraṃ vā padmaṃ trikoṇasaṃjñakam || 91 ||
4.d:
वृद्धावङ्गुलमङ्गुल्या षड्विंशाङ्गुलिकावधि ।
वृत्तं वा चतुरस्रं वा पद्मं त्रिकोणसंज्ञकम् ॥ 91 ॥
4.m: In enlargement, finger-breadth by finger-breadth up to twenty-six finger-breadths, / it may be circular or quadrangular, a lotus, or termed triangular.

4.s:
ratneśān padmamadhye tu gomuṣṭikavināyakaiḥ |
śrīśrīvṛkṣavarārohāmumādevīṃ śubhānvitām || 92 ||
4.d:
रत्नेशान् पद्ममध्ये तु गोमुष्टिकविनायकैः ।
श्रीश्रीवृक्षवरारोहामुमादेवीं शुभान्विताम् ॥ 92 ॥
4.m: The lords of jewels in the middle of the lotus, with gomuṣṭika and Vināyaka, / the auspicious goddess Umā, beautiful, [adorned with] śrī and the śrīvṛkṣa—

4.s:
ratnaiḥ sarvairalaṅkāraiḥ paṭṭaṃ kāryaṃ dvihastakam |
hastavistāramucchrāyaṃ navahastaṃ daśāṅgulam || 93 ||
4.d:
रत्नैः सर्वैरलङ्कारैः पट्टं कार्यं द्विहस्तकम् ।
हस्तविस्तारमुच्छ्रायं नवहस्तं दशाङ्गुलम् ॥ 93 ॥
4.m: with all jewels and ornaments, a board of two cubits should be made; / its width is a cubit and its height is nine cubits and ten finger-breadths.

4.s:
snānārthaṃ sārdhahastaṃ ca paṭṭaṃ vṛttaṃ guṇānvitam |
śayyā caturguṇā dīrghā dhanurmānaṃ tu pīṭhakam || 94 ||
4.d:
स्नानार्थं सार्धहस्तं च पट्टं वृत्तं गुणान्वितम् ।
शय्या चतुर्गुणा दीर्घा धनुर्मानं तु पीठकम् ॥ 94 ॥
4.m: And for the bath, a circular board of one and a half cubits, endowed with qualities; / a bed four times as long, and a stool measuring a bow.

4.s:
gajasiṃhakṛtāṭopaṃ hemaratnavibhūṣitam |
siṃhākhyaṃ sārdhavistārād daṇḍāsanamathāpi vā || 95 ||
4.d:
गजसिंहकृताटोपं हेमरत्नविभूषितम् ।
सिंहाख्यं सार्धविस्ताराद् दण्डासनमथापि वा ॥ 95 ॥
4.m: Displaying the grandeur of elephants and lions, adorned with gold and jewels, / called a throne, one and a half [cubits] in breadth, or a daṇḍāsana;

4.s:
vyāghracitrakapaṭṭairvā upadhānāni kārayet |
anyairvā nirmitāṃ carmamṛdutūlakapūritā || 96 ||
4.d:
व्याघ्रचित्रकपट्टैर्वा उपधानानि कारयेत् ।
अन्यैर्वा निर्मितां चर्ममृदुतूलकपूरिता ॥ 96 ॥
4.m: or one should make cushions of tiger-patterned silk / or made of other hides, filled with soft cotton.

4.s:
śayyā dīrghārghavistīrṇā caturhastā sulakṣaṇā |
vitastyadhikamicchanti nṛpasya guruvidyayā || 97 ||
4.d:
शय्या दीर्घार्घविस्तीर्णा चतुर्हस्ता सुलक्षणा ।
वितस्त्यधिकमिच्छन्ति नृपस्य गुरुविद्यया ॥ 97 ॥
4.m: A bed four cubits long and half as wide, possessing auspicious marks; / according to the wisdom of the king's guru, they desire it longer by a span.

4.s:
ardhacandrasamaṃ kuryādāsanaṃ caturasrakam |
upadhānāni śayyāyāḥ karṇādimūlabhedataḥ || 98 ||
4.d:
अर्धचन्द्रसमं कुर्यादासनं चतुरस्रकम् ।
उपधानानि शय्यायाः कर्णादिमूलभेदतः ॥ 98 ॥
4.m: One should make the seat four-cornered, resembling a half-moon; / the pillows of the bed, distinguished by head and foot,

4.s:
ṣoḍaśaivātra kāryāṇi varṇacitrayutāni ca |
yānaṃ siṃhāsana paṭṭaṃ śayyopakaraṇādikam || 99 ||
4.d:
षोडशैवात्र कार्याणि वर्णचित्रयुतानि च ।
यानं सिंहासन पट्टं शय्योपकरणादिकम् ॥ 99 ॥
4.m: are to be made sixteen in number here, endowed with colourful designs. / The vehicle, the lion-throne, the board, the bed furnishings, and so forth,

4.s:
rājño nūtanayogyaṃ tad vedyā uttarato nyaset |
teṣāṃ tu paścime svarṇaratnaughakhacite vare || 100 ||
4.d:
राज्ञो नूतनयोग्यं तद् वेद्या उत्तरतो न्यसेत् ।
तेषां तु पश्चिमे स्वर्णरत्नौघखचिते वरे ॥ 100 ॥
4.m: suited to be new for the king, he should place to the north of the altar; / and to the west of them, upon an excellent,

4.s:
paryaṅke yajñadārvaughanirmite mahadāstare |
rdhācchādanasaṃyukte carmāvṛtacatuṣṭaye || 101 ||
4.d:
पर्यङ्के यज्ञदार्वौघनिर्मिते महदास्तरे ।
र्धाच्छादनसंयुक्ते चर्मावृतचतुष्टये ॥ 101 ॥
4.m: spacious couch inlaid with a mass of gold and jewels, / made from a collection of sacrificial timber, provided with half-covering, draped with four skins—

4.s:
vṛṣabhasya tathorṇāyāḥ siṃhaśārdulayorapi |
pādapīṭhe ratnayute pādāvāropya pārthivaḥ || 102 ||
4.d:
वृषभस्य तथोर्णायाः सिंहशार्दुलयोरपि ।
पादपीठे रत्नयुते पादावारोप्य पार्थिवः ॥ 102 ॥
4.m: of a bull, of wool, and of a lion and a tiger; / having placed both feet upon the footstool adorned with jewels,

4.s:
asmin paryaṅkapīṭhasthe carmāvṛtacatuṣṭaya |
nānālaṅkārabhūṣāḍhyaṃ nṛpatiṃ ratnaśālinam || 103 ||
4.d:
अस्मिन् पर्यङ्कपीठस्थे चर्मावृतचतुष्टय ।
नानालङ्कारभूषाढ्यं नृपतिं रत्नशालिनम् ॥ 103 ॥
4.m: the king, seated upon this couch-pedestal draped with the four skins, / rich in diverse ornaments and adornments, resplendent with gems,

4.s:
snāpayed brāhmaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ rājānaṃ sukhasaṅgatam |
saṃvitakambalaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ ahuvastraiśca śaubhitam || 104 ||
4.d:
स्नापयेद् ब्राह्मणैः सार्धं राजानं सुखसङ्गतम् ।
संवितकम्बलं कृष्णं अहुवस्त्रैश्च शौभितम् ॥ 104 ॥
4.m: should bathe together with the brahmins, attained to ease, / wrapped in a black blanket and graced with many garments.

4.s:
kalasevalipuṣpādyaiḥ sālicūrṇaiśca snāpayet |
ṣṭau ṣauḍaśa viṃśāṣṭaśatamadhikaṃ ca vā || 105 ||
4.d:
कलसेवलिपुष्पाद्यैः सालिचूर्णैश्च स्नापयेत् ।
ष्टौ षौडश विंशाष्टशतमधिकं च वा ॥ 105 ॥
4.m: He should bathe with jars, offerings, flowers, and powders of śāli rice, / [using] eight, sixteen, twenty-eight, or a hundred [jars], or even more.

4.s:
kalasānāṃ samākhyātā adhikasyottarottaram |
jayakalyāṇadairmantrairmaṅgalotthaiśca śāmbhavaiḥ || 106 ||
4.d:
कलसानां समाख्याता अधिकस्योत्तरोत्तरम् ।
जयकल्याणदैर्मन्त्रैर्मङ्गलोत्थैश्च शाम्भवैः ॥ 106 ॥
4.m: [The numbers] of jars are declared, each greater [in number bringing] higher and higher [results], / with mantras granting victory and welfare, arising from blessings and dedicated to Śiva,

4.s:
vaiṣṇavairatha dikpālairgrahamantraiśca mātṛkaiḥ |
ājyaṃ tejaḥ samuddṛṣṭamājyaṃ pāpaharaṃ param || 107 ||
4.d:
वैष्णवैरथ दिक्पालैर्ग्रहमन्त्रैश्च मातृकैः ।
आज्यं तेजः समुद्दृष्टमाज्यं पापहरं परम् ॥ 107 ॥
4.m: dedicated to Viṣṇu, to the guardians of the directions, planetary mantras, and mothers' mantras: / Ghee is declared to be splendor; ghee is the supreme destroyer of sin;

4.s:
ājyaṃ surāṇāmāhāraprājye lokāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ |
haumāntarikṣaṃ divyaṃ vā yat te kalpamaṣamāgatam || 108 ||
4.d:
आज्यं सुराणामाहारप्राज्ये लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः ।
हौमान्तरिक्षं दिव्यं वा यत् ते कल्पमषमागतम् ॥ 108 ॥
4.m: ghee is the food of the gods; upon ghee the worlds are established. / Whatever defilement has befallen you—terrestrial, intermediate, or celestial—

4.s:
sarvaṃ tadājyasaṃsparśāt praṇāśamupagacchatu |
tato'panīyagātrāt tu kambalaṃ vastrameva ca || 109 ||
4.d:
सर्वं तदाज्यसंस्पर्शात् प्रणाशमुपगच्छतु ।
ततोऽपनीयगात्रात् तु कम्बलं वस्त्रमेव च ॥ 109 ॥
4.m: let all that perish through the contact of ghee! / Then, having removed the blanket and cloth from his body,

4.s:
kalasaiḥ snāpayed bhūpaṃ puṣpasnānīyapūritaiḥ |
ebhairmantrairnaraśreṣṭha tanutattvārthasādhakaiḥ || 110 ||
4.d:
कलसैः स्नापयेद् भूपं पुष्पस्नानीयपूरितैः ।
एभैर्मन्त्रैर्नरश्रेष्ठ तनुतत्त्वार्थसाधकैः ॥ 110 ॥
4.m: he should bathe the king with jars filled with fragrant bath-waters and flowers, / with these mantras, O best of men, which achieve the true reality of the body:

4.s:
urāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu ye ca siddhāḥ purātanāḥ |
brahmā viṣṇuśca rudrāśca sādhyāśca samarudgaṇāḥ || 111 ||
4.d:
उरास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु ये च सिद्धाः पुरातनाः ।
ब्रह्मा विष्णुश्च रुद्राश्च साध्याश्च समरुद्गणाः ॥ 111 ॥
4.m: ‘Let the gods consecrate you, and those who are ancient Siddhas, / Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and the Rudras, the Sādhyas together with the host of Maruts,

4.s:
ādityā vasavo rudrā aśvinau yo bhiṣagvarau |
aditirdevamātā ca svāhā lakṣmīḥ sarasvatī || 112 ||
4.d:
आदित्या वसवो रुद्रा अश्विनौ यो भिषग्वरौ ।
अदितिर्देवमाता च स्वाहा लक्ष्मीः सरस्वती ॥ 112 ॥
4.m: the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Aśvins who are the best of physicians, / Aditi the mother of the gods, Svāhā, Lakṣmī, and Sarasvatī,

4.s:
kīrtirlakṣmīrghṛtiḥ śrīśca sinīvālī kuhūstathā |
ditiśca surasā caiva vinatā kadrureva ca || 113 ||
4.d:
कीर्तिर्लक्ष्मीर्घृतिः श्रीश्च सिनीवाली कुहूस्तथा ।
दितिश्च सुरसा चैव विनता कद्रुरेव च ॥ 113 ॥
4.m: Kīrti, Lakṣmī, Dhṛti, and Śrī, Sinīvālī and Kuhū, / Diti, Surasā, Vinatā, and Kadrū,

4.s:
devapatnayaśca yāḥ proktā devamātara eva ca |
sarvāstvāmaṣiñcantu siddhāścāpsrasāṃ gaṇāḥ || 114 ||
4.d:
देवपत्नयश्च याः प्रोक्ता देवमातर एव च ।
सर्वास्त्वामषिञ्चन्तु सिद्धाश्चाप्स्रसां गणाः ॥ 114 ॥
4.m: and those who are declared the wives of the gods, and the mothers of the gods— / let them all consecrate you, and the Siddhas and troops of Apsarases;

4.s:
nakṣatrāṇi muhūrtāśca pakṣāhorātrasandhayaḥ |
saṃvatsarā nimeṣāśca kalāḥ kāṣṭhāḥ kṣaṇā lavāḥ || 115 ||
4.d:
नक्षत्राणि मुहूर्ताश्च पक्षाहोरात्रसन्धयः ।
संवत्सरा निमेषाश्च कलाः काष्ठाः क्षणा लवाः ॥ 115 ॥
4.m: the lunar mansions, the muhūrtas, the fortnights, the junctions of day and night, / the years, the twinklings of the eye, kalās, kāṣṭhās, kṣaṇas, and lavas—

4.s:
sarve tvāmabhiṣiñcantu kālasyāvayavastathā |
vaimānikāḥ suragaṇā manavaḥ sāgaraiḥ saha || 116 ||
4.d:
सर्वे त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु कालस्यावयवस्तथा ।
वैमानिकाः सुरगणा मनवः सागरैः सह ॥ 116 ॥
4.m: let all the divisions of time likewise consecrate you; / the sky-faring hosts of gods, the Manus together with the oceans,

4.s:
saritaśca mahānāgā nāgāḥ kiṃpuruṣāstathā |
vaikhānasā mahābhāgā dvijā vaihāyasāśca ye || 117 ||
4.d:
सरितश्च महानागा नागाः किंपुरुषास्तथा ।
वैखानसा महाभागा द्विजा वैहायसाश्च ये ॥ 117 ॥
4.m: the rivers, the great Nāgas, the snakes, and the Kimpuruṣas, / the most fortunate Vaikhānasa twice-born, and those who dwell in the sky;

4.s:
saptarṣayaḥ sadārāśca dhruvasthānāni yāni tu |
marīciratriḥ pulahaḥ pulastyaḥ kraturaṅgirāḥ || 118 ||
4.d:
सप्तर्षयः सदाराश्च ध्रुवस्थानानि यानि तु ।
मरीचिरत्रिः पुलहः पुलस्त्यः क्रतुरङ्गिराः ॥ 118 ॥
4.m: the Seven Rṣis together with their wives, and the fixed stations [of the heavens]: / Marīci, Atri, Pulaha, Pulastya, Kratu, Aṅgiras,

4.s:
bhṛguḥ sanatkumāraśca sanakaśca sanandanaḥ |
sanātanaśca dakṣaśca jaigīṣavyo'bhinandanaḥ || 119 ||
4.d:
भृगुः सनत्कुमारश्च सनकश्च सनन्दनः ।
सनातनश्च दक्षश्च जैगीषव्योऽभिनन्दनः ॥ 119 ॥
4.m: Bhṛgu, Sanatkumāra, Sanaka, Sanandana, / Sanātana, Dakṣa, Jaigīṣavya, Abhinandana,

4.s:
ekataśca dvitaścaiva trito jāvālikāśyapau |
durvāsā durvinītaśca kaṇvaḥ kātyāyanastathā || 120 ||
4.d:
एकतश्च द्वितश्चैव त्रितो जावालिकाश्यपौ ।
दुर्वासा दुर्विनीतश्च कण्वः कात्यायनस्तथा ॥ 120 ॥
4.m: Ekata, Dvita, and Trita, Jābāli, Kāśyapa, / Durvāsas, Durvinīta, Kaṇva, and Kātyāyana,

4.s:
mārkaṇḍeyo dīrghatamāḥ śunaḥśepho vidūrathaḥ |
aurvaḥ saṃvartakaścaiva cyavano'triḥ parāśaraḥ || 121 ||
4.d:
मार्कण्डेयो दीर्घतमाः शुनःशेफो विदूरथः ।
और्वः संवर्तकश्चैव च्यवनोऽत्रिः पराशरः ॥ 121 ॥
4.m: Mārkaṇḍeya, Dīrghatamas, Śunaḥśepha, Vidūratha, / Aurva, Saṃvartaka, Cyavana, Atri, Parāśara,

4.s:
dvaipāyano yavakrīto devarātaḥ sahātmajaḥ |
ete cānye ca bahavo vedavrataparāyaṇāḥ || 122 ||
4.d:
द्वैपायनो यवक्रीतो देवरातः सहात्मजः ।
एते चान्ये च बहवो वेदव्रतपरायणाः ॥ 122 ॥
4.m: Dvaipāyana, Yavakrīta, and Devarāta with his son— / these and many others devoted to the Vedic vows,

4.s:
saśiṣyāste'bhiṣiñcantu sadārāśca tapodhanāḥ |
parvatāstaravo nadyaḥ puṇyānyāyatatanāni ca || 123 ||
4.d:
सशिष्यास्तेऽभिषिञ्चन्तु सदाराश्च तपोधनाः ।
पर्वतास्तरवो नद्यः पुण्यान्यायततनानि च ॥ 123 ॥
4.m: rich in austerities, accompanied by disciples and wives, consecrate you! / The mountains, trees, rivers, and holy shrines,

4.s:
prajāpatiḥ kṣitiścaiva gāvo viśvasya mātaraḥ |
vāhanāni ca divyāni sarve lokāścarācarāḥ || 124 ||
4.d:
प्रजापतिः क्षितिश्चैव गावो विश्वस्य मातरः ।
वाहनानि च दिव्यानि सर्वे लोकाश्चराचराः ॥ 124 ॥
4.m: Prajāpati, the earth, the cows that are the mothers of the universe, / the divine vehicles, and all the worlds moving and unmoving;

4.s:
agnayaḥ pitarastārā jīmūtāḥ khaṃ diśo jalam |
ete cānye ca bahavaḥ puṇyasaṃkīrtanāḥ śubhāḥ || 125 ||
4.d:
अग्नयः पितरस्तारा जीमूताः खं दिशो जलम् ।
एते चान्ये च बहवः पुण्यसंकीर्तनाः शुभाः ॥ 125 ॥
4.m: the fires, ancestors, stars, rain-clouds, sky, directions, and water— / these and many other auspicious beings of holy renown,

4.s:
toyaistvāmabhiṣiñcantu sarvotpātanibarhaṇaiḥ |
ityevaṃ śubhadairetairdivyarmantraistathāparaiḥ || 126 ||
4.d:
तोयैस्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु सर्वोत्पातनिबर्हणैः ।
इत्येवं शुभदैरेतैर्दिव्यर्मन्त्रैस्तथापरैः ॥ 126 ॥
4.m: consecrate you with waters that destroy all portents!’ / Thus with these auspicious divine mantras and with others,

4.s:
sorairnārāyaṇai raudrairbahmaśakrasamudbhavaiḥ |
āpohiṣṭhā hiraṇyeti sambhaveti sureti ca || 127 ||
4.d:
सोरैर्नारायणै रौद्रैर्बह्मशक्रसमुद्भवैः ।
आपोहिष्ठा हिरण्येति सम्भवेति सुरेति च ॥ 127 ॥
4.m: addressed to the Sun, to Nārāyaṇa, to Rudra, and those arising from Brahmā and Indra; / with ‘Āpo hi ṣṭhā’, ‘Hiraṇya…’, ‘Saṃbhavet…’, ‘Surā…’,

4.s:
mānastoketi mantreṇa gandhadvāretyanena ca |
sarvamaṃgalamāṃgalye śrīśca te grahayogibhiḥ || 118 ||
4.d:
मानस्तोकेति मन्त्रेण गन्धद्वारेत्यनेन च ।
सर्वमंगलमांगल्ये श्रीश्च ते ग्रहयोगिभिः ॥ 118 ॥
4.m: with the mantra ‘Mā nas toke…’, and with ‘Gandhadvārā…’, / ‘Sarvamaṅgalamāṅgalye…’, and ‘Śrīś ca te…’, accompanied by planetary rites;

4.s:
ityevaṃ snānamāsādya gātramāvṛtya kambalaiḥ |
sarvamaṃgalamantreṇa vastraṃ kārpāsakaṃ dhriyāt || 129 ||
4.d:
इत्येवं स्नानमासाद्य गात्रमावृत्य कम्बलैः ।
सर्वमंगलमन्त्रेण वस्त्रं कार्पासकं ध्रियात् ॥ 129 ॥
4.m: thus having performed the bath and covered his body with blankets, / he should put on a cotton garment with the all-auspicious mantra.

4.s:
ācamya ca tato devān guruṃ viprāṃśca pūjayet |
dhvajacchatraṃ cāmaraṃ ca ghaṇṭāṃ cāśvān gajāṃstathā || 130 ||
4.d:
आचम्य च ततो देवान् गुरुं विप्रांश्च पूजयेत् ।
ध्वजच्छत्रं चामरं च घण्टां चाश्वान् गजांस्तथा ॥ 130 ॥
4.m: Then, having sipped water, he should worship the gods, the guru, and the brāhmaṇas; / and muttering the mantra over the banner, parasol, chowrie, bell, horses, and elephants,

4.s:
mantraṃ japtvā dhārayet tu tato gaccheddhutāśanam |
tatra gatvā vahnimadhye vahneḥ śrīrvīkṣya pārthivaḥ || 131 ||
4.d:
मन्त्रं जप्त्वा धारयेत् तु ततो गच्छेद्धुताशनम् ।
तत्र गत्वा वह्निमध्ये वह्नेः श्रीर्वीक्ष्य पार्थिवः ॥ 131 ॥
4.m: he should bear them, and then approach the fire. / Having gone there, the king, beholding the glory of the fire within the fire,

4.s:
imittānyanimittāni lakṣayet tatra bindubhiḥ |
daivajñakañcukyamātyavandipaurajanairvṛtaḥ || 132 ||
4.d:
इमित्तान्यनिमित्तानि लक्षयेत् तत्र बिन्दुभिः ।
दैवज्ञकञ्चुक्यमात्यवन्दिपौरजनैर्वृतः ॥ 132 ॥
4.m: should observe the auspicious and inauspicious omens there by means of the sparks, / surrounded by the astrologer, chamberlains, ministers, bards, and citizens.

4.s:
vāditraghoṣaistumalaistathā tauryatrikaiḥ śubhaiḥ |
kṛtvā śeṣe punaḥ śāntimāśīrvācya ca vai dvijān || 133 ||
4.d:
वादित्रघोषैस्तुमलैस्तथा तौर्यत्रिकैः शुभैः ।
कृत्वा शेषे पुनः शान्तिमाशीर्वाच्य च वै द्विजान् ॥ 133 ॥
4.m: With tumultuous sounds of musical instruments and auspicious threefold instrumental music, / having performed the pacificatory rite again at the conclusion and had the twice-born pronounce blessings,

4.s:
pūrṇāṃ vidhāya vidhivad dakṣiṇāṃ kanakānvitām |
dhānyāni cātha vāsāṃsi dattvā kuryād visarjanam || 134 ||
4.d:
पूर्णां विधाय विधिवद् दक्षिणां कनकान्विताम् ।
धान्यानि चाथ वासांसि दत्त्वा कुर्याद् विसर्जनम् ॥ 134 ॥
4.m: having offered the final oblation according to rule, and given the priestly fee along with gold, / grains, and garments, he should perform the dismissal.

4.s:
tataḥ śeṣajalaiḥ sarvānamātyādīn purohitaḥ |
secayeccaturaṅgaṃ ca balaṃ cāpi sarāṣṭrakam || 135 ||
4.d:
ततः शेषजलैः सर्वानमात्यादीन् पुरोहितः ।
सेचयेच्चतुरङ्गं च बलं चापि सराष्ट्रकम् ॥ 135 ॥
4.m: Then, with the remaining waters, the royal priest should sprinkle / all the ministers and others, and the fourfold army along with the realm.

4.s:
evaṃ kṛtvā nṛpaḥ paścāt trirātraṃ saṃyato bhavet |
māṃsamaithunahīnaśca kuryānmāṅgalyasevanam || 136 ||
4.d:
एवं कृत्वा नृपः पश्चात् त्रिरात्रं संयतो भवेत् ।
मांसमैथुनहीनश्च कुर्यान्माङ्गल्यसेवनम् ॥ 136 ॥
4.m: Having done this, the king should subsequently remain self-restrained for three nights; / refraining from meat and sexual intercourse, he should perform auspicious practices.

4.s:
puṣyanakṣatrayuktā tu tṛtīyā yadi labhyate |
tasyāṃ pūjyā sadā devī caṇḍikā śaṃkareṇa ha || 137 ||
4.d:
पुष्यनक्षत्रयुक्ता तु तृतीया यदि लभ्यते ।
तस्यां पूज्या सदा देवी चण्डिका शंकरेण ह ॥ 137 ॥
4.m: If the third lunar day is conjoined with the constellation Puṣya, / on that day the goddess Caṇḍikā should always be worshipped together with Śaṅkara.

4.s:
pāñcālikāvihārādyaiḥ śiśūnāṃ kautukaistathā |
vaivāhikena vidhinā mohayeccaṇḍikāṃ śivām || 138 ||
4.d:
पाञ्चालिकाविहाराद्यैः शिशूनां कौतुकैस्तथा ।
वैवाहिकेन विधिना मोहयेच्चण्डिकां शिवाम् ॥ 138 ॥
4.m: With the play of dolls and the joyful sports of children, / and with the rites of marriage, one should delight Caṇḍikā, who is Śivā.

4.s:
catuṣpatheṣu sarveṣu devadevīgaheṣu ca |
patākābhiralaṃ kuryādevaṃ kurvanna sīdati || 139 ||
4.d:
चतुष्पथेषु सर्वेषु देवदेवीगहेषु च ।
पताकाभिरलं कुर्यादेवं कुर्वन्न सीदति ॥ 139 ॥
4.m: At all crossroads and in the temples of gods and goddesses, / he should decorate with flags; doing so, he never suffers distress.

4.s:
evaṃ kṛtvā śāntiyāgaṃ tathā puṣyābhiṣecanam |
caturaṅgaiḥ samaṃ rājā bhāryabhistu naraiḥ saha || 140 ||
4.d:
एवं कृत्वा शान्तियागं तथा पुष्याभिषेचनम् ।
चतुरङ्गैः समं राजा भार्यभिस्तु नरैः सह ॥ 140 ॥
4.m: Having thus performed the pacificatory sacrifice and the Puṣya-consecration, / the king, together with his fourfold army, his wives, and his men,

4.s:
rājyamaṇḍalasaṃyuktaḥ paratreha na sīdati |
nātaḥ parataro yajño nātaḥ paratarotsavaḥ || 141 ||
4.d:
राज्यमण्डलसंयुक्तः परत्रेह न सीदति ।
नातः परतरो यज्ञो नातः परतरोत्सवः ॥ 141 ॥
4.m: joined with the circle of his kingdom, does not suffer in the next world or in this. / There is no sacrifice higher than this; there is no festival higher than this;

4.s:
nātaḥ paratarā śāntirnātaḥ parataraṃ śivam |
anenaiva vidhānena nṛpaterabhiṣecanam || 142 ||
4.d:
नातः परतरा शान्तिर्नातः परतरं शिवम् ।
अनेनैव विधानेन नृपतेरभिषेचनम् ॥ 142 ॥
4.m: there is no appeasement higher than this; there is no welfare higher than this. / Following this very rite, the royal priest should perform

4.s:
yuvarājyābhiṣekaṃ ca kuryādrājapurohitaḥ |
nṛpābhiṣekakaraṇamādau yadi samācaret || 143 ||
4.d:
युवराज्याभिषेकं च कुर्याद्राजपुरोहितः ।
नृपाभिषेककरणमादौ यदि समाचरेत् ॥ 143 ॥
4.m: the consecration of a king and the consecration to heir-apparency. / If one performs the king's consecration at the outset

4.s:
anenaiva vidhānena sthiraḥ syānnṛpatistadā |
ayaṃ yajñaḥ samuddiṣṭaḥ śakrārthaṃ brahmaṇā purā |
evaṃ yajñaṃ nṛpaḥ kṛtvā paratreha na sīdati || 144 ||
4.d:
अनेनैव विधानेन स्थिरः स्यान्नृपतिस्तदा ।
अयं यज्ञः समुद्दिष्टः शक्रार्थं ब्रह्मणा पुरा ।
एवं यज्ञं नृपः कृत्वा परत्रेह न सीदति ॥ 144 ॥
4.m: by this very rite, then the king becomes established. / This sacrifice was ordained of old by Brahmā for the sake of Indra; / having performed such a sacrifice, a king does not suffer in this world or the next.

4.s: iti śrīkālikāpurāṇe ṣaḍaśītitamo'dhyāyaḥ || 86 ||
4.d: इति श्रीकालिकापुराणे षडशीतितमोऽध्यायः ॥ 86 ॥
4.m: Thus ends the eighty-sixth chapter in the glorious Kālikāpurāṇa.

4.s: saptāśītitamo'dhyāyaḥ
4.d: सप्ताशीतितमोऽध्यायः
4.m: Eighty-seventh Chapter

4.s: aurva uvāca -
4.d: और्व उवाच -

4.s:
athātaḥ śṛṇu rājendra śakotthānaṃ dhvajotsavam |
yat kṛtvā nṛpatiryāti na kadācit parābhavam || 1 ||
4.d:
अथातः शृणु राजेन्द्र शकोत्थानं ध्वजोत्सवम् ।
यत् कृत्वा नृपतिर्याति न कदाचित् पराभवम् ॥ 1 ॥
4.m: Now hear, O king of kings, the raising of Indra's staff and the flag festival, / having performed which a king never meets with defeat.

4.s:
ravau haristhe dvādaśyāṃ śravaṇena viḍaujasam |
arādhayennapaḥ samyak sarvavighnopaśāntaye || 2 ||
4.d:
रवौ हरिस्थे द्वादश्यां श्रवणेन विडौजसम् ।
अराधयेन्नपः सम्यक् सर्वविघ्नोपशान्तये ॥ 2 ॥
4.m: When the sun is in Leo, on the twelfth lunar day with Śravaṇa, / the king should worship Indra properly for the pacification of all obstacles.

4.s:
rājoparircaro nāma vasunāmāparastu yaḥ |
nṛpastenāyamatulo yajñaḥ prāvartitaḥ purā || 3 ||
4.d:
राजोपरिर्चरो नाम वसुनामापरस्तु यः ।
नृपस्तेनायमतुलो यज्ञः प्रावर्तितः पुरा ॥ 3 ॥
4.m: The king named Uparicara, who was also named Vasu— / by that king this peerless sacrifice was instituted in ancient times.

4.s:
prāvṛṭkāle ca nabhasi dvādaśyāmasitetare |
purāhito vahuvidhairvādyastūryaiḥ samanvitaḥ || 4 ||
4.d:
प्रावृट्काले च नभसि द्वादश्यामसितेतरे ।
पुराहितो वहुविधैर्वाद्यस्तूर्यैः समन्वितः ॥ 4 ॥
4.m: In the rainy season, in the month of Nabhas, on the bright twelfth lunar day, / the royal priest, accompanied by various musical instruments and trumpets,

4.s:
prathamaṃ śakaketvartha vṛkṣamāmantrya vardhayet |
āṃvatsaro vārdhaṃkiśca kṛtamaṅgalakautukaḥ || 5 ||
4.d:
प्रथमं शककेत्वर्थ वृक्षमामन्त्र्य वर्धयेत् ।
आंवत्सरो वार्धंकिश्च कृतमङ्गलकौतुकः ॥ 5 ॥
4.m: First, for the purpose of Śakra's banner, the astrologer and the carpenter, / having performed auspicious rites, should address and fell a tree.

4.s:
udyāne devatāgāre śmaśāne mārgamadhyataḥ |
ye jātāstaravastāṃstu varjayed vāsavadhvaje || 6 ||
4.d:
उद्याने देवतागारे श्मशाने मार्गमध्यतः ।
ये जातास्तरवस्तांस्तु वर्जयेद् वासवध्वजे ॥ 6 ॥
4.m: Trees grown in a pleasure garden, a temple, a cremation ground, or the middle of a road / must be avoided for Vāsava's banner.

4.s:
bahuvallīyutaṃ śuṣkaṃ bahukaṇṭakasaṃyutam |
kubjaṃ vṛkṣādanīyuktaṃ latācchannataruaṃ tyajet || 7 ||
4.d:
बहुवल्लीयुतं शुष्कं बहुकण्टकसंयुतम् ।
कुब्जं वृक्षादनीयुक्तं लताच्छन्नतरुअं त्यजेत् ॥ 7 ॥
4.m: One should reject a tree covered in many creepers, withered, full of many thorns, / crooked, parasitized by mistletoe, or overgrown with vines.

4.s:
pakṣivāsasamākīrṇaṃ koṭarairbahubhiryutam |
pavanānalavidhvastaṃ taruṃ yatnena varjayet || 8 ||
4.d:
पक्षिवाससमाकीर्णं कोटरैर्बहुभिर्युतम् ।
पवनानलविध्वस्तं तरुं यत्नेन वर्जयेत् ॥ 8 ॥
4.m: One should diligently avoid a tree filled with birds' nests, / having many hollows, or damaged by wind and fire.

4.s:
nārīsaṃjñāśca ye vṛkṣā atihrasvā atikṛśāḥ |
tān sadā varjayed dhīraḥ sarvadā śakrapūjane || 9 ||
4.d:
नारीसंज्ञाश्च ये वृक्षा अतिह्रस्वा अतिकृशाः ।
तान् सदा वर्जयेद् धीरः सर्वदा शक्रपूजने ॥ 9 ॥
4.m: And trees with feminine names, very short ones, and very thin ones: / the wise man should always avoid them in the worship of Śakra.

4.s:
arjuno'pyaśvakarṇaśca vaṭaḥ priyakoṣaka śca |
audumbaraśca paṃcaite ketvarthe hyuttamāḥ smṛtāḥ || 10 ||
4.d:
अर्जुनोऽप्यश्वकर्णश्च वटः प्रियकोषक श्च ।
औदुम्बरश्च पंचैते केत्वर्थे ह्युत्तमाः स्मृताः ॥ 10 ॥
4.m: The arjuna, the aśvakarṇa, the banyan, the priyaka, / and the audumbara—these five are traditionally considered best for the banner.

4.s:
anye ca devadārvādyāḥ śālādyāstaravastathā |
praśastāstu parigrāhyā nāpraśastāḥ kadācana || 11 ||
4.d:
अन्ये च देवदार्वाद्याः शालाद्यास्तरवस्तथा ।
प्रशस्तास्तु परिग्राह्या नाप्रशस्ताः कदाचन ॥ 11 ॥
4.m: Other trees, such as the devadāru and the śāla, / if commendable, should be taken; uncommendable ones must never be taken.

4.s:
dhṛtvā vṛkṣaṃ tato rātrau spṛṣṭvā mantramimaṃ paṭhet |
yāni vṛkṣeṣu bhūtāni tebhyaḥ svasti namo'stu vaḥ || 12 ||
4.d:
धृत्वा वृक्षं ततो रात्रौ स्पृष्ट्वा मन्त्रमिमं पठेत् ।
यानि वृक्षेषु भूतानि तेभ्यः स्वस्ति नमोऽस्तु वः ॥ 12 ॥
4.m: Then, having approached the tree at night and touched it, he should recite this mantra: / 'Whatever spirits reside in trees, hail to them; homage be to you!

4.s:
upahāraṃ gṛhītvemaṃ kriyatāṃ vāsavadhvajam |
pārthivastvāṃ varayate svasti te'stu nagottama || 13 ||
4.d:
उपहारं गृहीत्वेमं क्रियतां वासवध्वजम् ।
पार्थिवस्त्वां वरयते स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु नगोत्तम ॥ 13 ॥
4.m: Accepting this offering, let Vāsava's banner be made! / The king chooses you; may hail be to you, best of trees!

4.s:
dhvajārthaṃ devarājasya pūjeyaṃ pratigṛhyatām |
tato'pare'hni taṃ chittvā mūlamaṣṭāṃgulaṃ punaḥ || 14 ||
4.d:
ध्वजार्थं देवराजस्य पूजेयं प्रतिगृह्यताम् ।
ततोऽपरेऽह्नि तं छित्त्वा मूलमष्टांगुलं पुनः ॥ 14 ॥
4.m: May this worship be accepted for the banner of the king of gods!' / Then, having felled it on the following day, cutting eight aṅgulas again from the base,

4.s:
jale kṣipet tathāgrasya chitvaiva caturaṅgulam |
tato nītvā puradvāraṃ ketuṃ nirmāya tatra vai || 15 ||
4.d:
जले क्षिपेत् तथाग्रस्य छित्वैव चतुरङ्गुलम् ।
ततो नीत्वा पुरद्वारं केतुं निर्माय तत्र वै ॥ 15 ॥
4.m: he should throw it into water, having cut four aṅgulas from the tip as well. / Then, bringing it to the city gate and fashioning the banner there,

4.s:
śuklāṣṭamyāṃ bhādrapade ketuṃ vedīṃ praveśayet |
dvāviṃśaddhastamānastu adhamaḥ keturucyate || 16 ||
4.d:
शुक्लाष्टम्यां भाद्रपदे केतुं वेदीं प्रवेशयेत् ।
द्वाविंशद्धस्तमानस्तु अधमः केतुरुच्यते ॥ 16 ॥
4.m: he should bring the banner to the sacrificial altar on the bright eighth of Bhādrapada. / A banner measuring twenty-two cubits is called the lowest;

4.s:
dvātriṃśat tu tato jyāyān dvācatvāriṃśadeva ca |
tato'dhikaḥ samākhyāto dvāpañcāśat tathottamaḥ || 17 ||
4.d:
द्वात्रिंशत् तु ततो ज्यायान् द्वाचत्वारिंशदेव च ।
ततोऽधिकः समाख्यातो द्वापञ्चाशत् तथोत्तमः ॥ 17 ॥
4.m: thirty-two cubits is superior to that; forty-two cubits / is declared greater than that; and fifty-two cubits is the best.

4.s:
kumāryaḥ pañca kartavyāḥ śakrasya nṛpasattama |
śalamayyastu tāḥ sarvā aparāḥ śakramātṛkāḥ || 18 ||
4.d:
कुमार्यः पञ्च कर्तव्याः शक्रस्य नृपसत्तम ।
शलमय्यस्तु ताः सर्वा अपराः शक्रमातृकाः ॥ 18 ॥
4.m: Five maidens should be made for Śakra, O best of kings, / all fashioned of śāla wood; and other figures called the Mothers of Śakra.

4.s:
ketoḥ pādapramāṇena kāryāḥ śakrakumārikāḥ |
mātṛkārdhapramāṇāstu yantraṃ hastadvayaṃ tathā || 19 ||
4.d:
केतोः पादप्रमाणेन कार्याः शक्रकुमारिकाः ।
मातृकार्धप्रमाणास्तु यन्त्रं हस्तद्वयं तथा ॥ 19 ॥
4.m: The maidens of Śakra should be made one-fourth the size of the banner, / the Mothers half that size, and the mechanism two cubits.

4.s:
evaṃ kṛtvā kumārīśca mātṛkāḥ ketumeva ca |
ekādaśyāṃ site pakṣe yaṣṭiṃ tāmadhivāsayet || 20 ||
4.d:
एवं कृत्वा कुमारीश्च मातृकाः केतुमेव च ।
एकादश्यां सिते पक्षे यष्टिं तामधिवासयेत् ॥ 20 ॥
4.m: Having thus made the maidens, the Mothers, and the banner itself, / he should consecrate that pole on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight.

4.s:
adhivāsya tato yaṣṭiṃ gandhadvārādimantrakaiḥ |
dvādaśyāṃ maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā vāsavaṃ vistṛtātmakam || 21 ||
4.d:
अधिवास्य ततो यष्टिं गन्धद्वारादिमन्त्रकैः ।
द्वादश्यां मण्डलं कृत्वा वासवं विस्तृतात्मकम् ॥ 21 ॥
4.m: Having then consecrated the pole with the mantras beginning with 'Gandhadvārā,' / and having drawn an extensive diagram of Vāsava on the twelfth,

4.s:
acyutaṃ pūjayitvā tu śakraṃ paścāt prapūjayet |
śakrasya pratimāṃ kuryāt kāñcanīṃ dākhīṃ ca vā || 22 ||
4.d:
अच्युतं पूजयित्वा तु शक्रं पश्चात् प्रपूजयेत् ।
शक्रस्य प्रतिमां कुर्यात् काञ्चनीं दाखीं च वा ॥ 22 ॥
4.m: he should first worship Acyuta and then worship Śakra. / He should make an image of Śakra out of gold or wood,

4.s:
anyataijasasambhūtāṃ sarvābhāve tu mṛnmayīm |
tāṃ maṇḍalasya madhye tu pūjayitvā viśeṣataḥ || 23 ||
4.d:
अन्यतैजससम्भूतां सर्वाभावे तु मृन्मयीम् ।
तां मण्डलस्य मध्ये तु पूजयित्वा विशेषतः ॥ 23 ॥
4.m: or produced from another metal, or of clay if none of these are available. / Having worshipped it especially in the center of the diagram,

4.s:
tataḥ śubhe muhūrte tu ketumutthāpayennṛpaḥ |
vajrahasta surārughna bahunetra purandara |
kṣemārthaṃ sarvalokānāṃ pūjeyaṃ pratigṛhyatām || 24 ||
4.d:
ततः शुभे मुहूर्ते तु केतुमुत्थापयेन्नृपः ।
वज्रहस्त सुरारुघ्न बहुनेत्र पुरन्दर ।
क्षेमार्थं सर्वलोकानां पूजेयं प्रतिगृह्यताम् ॥ 24 ॥
4.m: the king should then raise the banner at an auspicious moment: / 'O holder of the thunderbolt, destroyer of the enemies of gods, thousand-eyed Purandara! / May this worship be accepted for the welfare of all the worlds.

4.s:
ehyehi sarvāmarasiddhasaṅghairabhiṣṭuto vajradharāmareśa |
samutthitastvaṃ śravaṇādyapāde gṛhāṇa pūjāṃ bhagavannamaste || 25 ||
4.d:
एह्येहि सर्वामरसिद्धसङ्घैरभिष्टुतो वज्रधरामरेश ।
समुत्थितस्त्वं श्रवणाद्यपादे गृहाण पूजां भगवन्नमस्ते ॥ 25 ॥
4.m: Come, come, O thunderbolt-wielder praised by all assemblies of gods and siddhas, lord of immortals! / Raised during the first quarter of Śravaṇā, accept the worship, O Blessed One; homage to you!'

4.s:
evamuttaratantroktairdahanaplavanādibhiḥ |
iti mantreṇa tantreṇa nānāmaivedyavedanaiḥ || 26 ||
4.d:
एवमुत्तरतन्त्रोक्तैर्दहनप्लवनादिभिः ।
इति मन्त्रेण तन्त्रेण नानामैवेद्यवेदनैः ॥ 26 ॥
4.m: Thus, with burning, flooding, and so forth as prescribed in the higher tantra, / with this mantra and ritual procedure, with announcements of various offerings,

4.s:
apapaiḥ pāyasaiḥ pānairguḍairdhānābhireva ca |
bhakṣyairbhojyaiśca vividhaiḥ pūjayecchrīvivṛddhaye || 27 ||
4.d:
अपपैः पायसैः पानैर्गुडैर्धानाभिरेव च ।
भक्ष्यैर्भोज्यैश्च विविधैः पूजयेच्छ्रीविवृद्धये ॥ 27 ॥
4.m: with cakes, milk-rice, drinks, jaggery, parched grains, / and various kinds of edible foods, he should worship for the increase of prosperity.

4.s:
ghaṭe tu daśadikpālān grahāṃśca paripūjayet |
sādhyādīn sakalān devān mātṛḥ sarvā anukramāt || 28 ||
4.d:
घटे तु दशदिक्पालान् ग्रहांश्च परिपूजयेत् ।
साध्यादीन् सकलान् देवान् मातृः सर्वा अनुक्रमात् ॥ 28 ॥
4.m: In a pot he should worship the guardians of the ten directions and the planets, / all the gods such as the Sādhyas, and all the Mothers in order.

4.s:
tataḥ śubhe muhūrte tu jñānivardhakisaṃyutaḥ |
ketūtthāpanabhūmiṃ tu yajñavedyāstu paścime || 29 ||
4.d:
ततः शुभे मुहूर्ते तु ज्ञानिवर्धकिसंयुतः ।
केतूत्थापनभूमिं तु यज्ञवेद्यास्तु पश्चिमे ॥ 29 ॥
4.m: Then, at an auspicious moment, accompanied by wise men and carpenters, / to the ground for raising the banner to the west of the sacrificial altar,

4.s:
vipraiḥ purohitaiḥ sārdhaṃ gacchedrājā sumaṃgalaiḥ |
rajjubhiḥ paṃcabhirbaddhaṃ yantraśliṣṭaṃ samātṛkam || 30 ||
4.d:
विप्रैः पुरोहितैः सार्धं गच्छेद्राजा सुमंगलैः ।
रज्जुभिः पंचभिर्बद्धं यन्त्रश्लिष्टं समातृकम् ॥ 30 ॥
4.m: the king should go together with brāhmaṇas and priests, amidst auspicious omens. / Bound with five ropes, fitted with the mechanism, accompanied by the Mothers,

4.s:
kumārībhistu saṃyuktaṃ dikpālānāṃ ca paṭṭakaiḥ |
bṛhadbhiratikāntaiśca nānādravyaiḥ supūritaiḥ || 31 ||
4.d:
कुमारीभिस्तु संयुक्तं दिक्पालानां च पट्टकैः ।
बृहद्भिरतिकान्तैश्च नानाद्रव्यैः सुपूरितैः ॥ 31 ॥
4.m: joined with the maidens, and [bearing] the banners of the guardians of the directions, / large, exceedingly lovely, and fully stocked with various articles,

4.s:
yathāvarṇairyathādeśe yojitairvastraveṣṭitaiḥ |
yuktaṃ taṃ kiṅkiṇījālairbṛhadghaṇṭaughacāmarai || 32 ||
4.d:
यथावर्णैर्यथादेशे योजितैर्वस्त्रवेष्टितैः ।
युक्तं तं किङ्किणीजालैर्बृहद्घण्टौघचामरै ॥ 32 ॥
4.m: arranged according to their colors in their proper places, wrapped with cloth, / fitted with clusters of small bells, heaps of large bells, and fly-whisks,

4.s:
bhūṣitaṃ mukurairucciarmālyairbahuvidhaistathā |
bahupuṣpaiḥ sugandhaiśca bhūṣitaṃ ratnamālayā || 33 ||
4.d:
भूषितं मुकुरैरुच्चिअर्माल्यैर्बहुविधैस्तथा ।
बहुपुष्पैः सुगन्धैश्च भूषितं रत्नमालया ॥ 33 ॥
4.m: adorned with mirrors on high, and likewise with various kinds of garlands, / with many fragrant flowers, and adorned with a string of jewels,

4.s:
citamālyāmbaraiścaiva caturbhirapi toraṇaiḥ |
utthāpayenmahāketuṃ rājakīyai śanaiḥ śanaiḥ || 34 ||
4.d:
चितमाल्याम्बरैश्चैव चतुर्भिरपि तोरणैः ।
उत्थापयेन्महाकेतुं राजकीयै शनैः शनैः ॥ 34 ॥
4.m: and with four archways hung with varied garlands and cloths, / the royal attendants should raise the great banner very slowly.

4.s:
tamutthāya mahāketuṃ pūjitaṃ maṇḍalāntare |
pratimāṃ tāṃ nayenmūlaṃ ketoḥ śakraṃ vicintayan || 35 ||
4.d:
तमुत्थाय महाकेतुं पूजितं मण्डलान्तरे ।
प्रतिमां तां नयेन्मूलं केतोः शक्रं विचिन्तयन् ॥ 35 ॥
4.m: Having raised that great banner worshipped in the center of the diagram, / he should bring that image to the base of the banner, meditating upon Śakra.

4.s:
yajet taṃ pūrvavat tatra śacīṃ mātalimeva ca |
jayantaṃ tanayaṃ tasya vajramairāvataṃ tathā || 36 ||
4.d:
यजेत् तं पूर्ववत् तत्र शचीं मातलिमेव च ।
जयन्तं तनयं तस्य वज्रमैरावतं तथा ॥ 36 ॥
4.m: He should worship him there as before, and Śacī, and Mātali, / and his son Jayanta, as well as the thunderbolt and Airāvata,

4.s:
grahāṃścāpyatha dikpālān sarvāśca gaṇadevatāḥ |
apūpādyaiḥ pūtayet tu valibhiḥ pāyasādibhiḥ || 37 ||
4.d:
ग्रहांश्चाप्यथ दिक्पालान् सर्वाश्च गणदेवताः ।
अपूपाद्यैः पूतयेत् तु वलिभिः पायसादिभिः ॥ 37 ॥
4.m: and the planets, the guardians of the directions, and all the host-deities; / he should purify them with cakes, offerings, milk-rice, and the like.

4.s:
pūjitānāṃ ca devānāṃ śaśvaddhomaṃ samācaret |
homānte tu baliṃ dadyād vāsavāya mahātmane || 38 ||
4.d:
पूजितानां च देवानां शश्वद्धोमं समाचरेत् ।
होमान्ते तु बलिं दद्याद् वासवाय महात्मने ॥ 38 ॥
4.m: He should continuously perform oblations for the worshipped deities; / at the end of the oblation he should offer a tribute to the great-souled Vāsava.

4.s:
tilaṃ ghṛtaṃ cākṣataṃ ca pūṣpaṃ dūrvāṃ tathaiva ca |
etaistu juhuyād devān svaiḥ svairmantrairnarottama || 39 ||
4.d:
तिलं घृतं चाक्षतं च पूष्पं दूर्वां तथैव च ।
एतैस्तु जुहुयाद् देवान् स्वैः स्वैर्मन्त्रैर्नरोत्तम ॥ 39 ॥
4.m: With sesamum, clarified butter, unbroken rice, flowers, and dūrvā grass— / with these he should make oblations to the deities with their respective mantras, O best of men.

4.s:
tato homāvasāne tu bhojayed brāhmaṇānapi |
evaṃ sampūjayennityaṃ saptarātraṃ dine dine || 40 ||
4.d:
ततो होमावसाने तु भोजयेद् ब्राह्मणानपि ।
एवं सम्पूजयेन्नित्यं सप्तरात्रं दिने दिने ॥ 40 ॥
4.m: Then, at the conclusion of the oblation, he should feed the brāhmaṇas. / Thus he should worship regularly day after day for seven nights.

4.s:
brāhmaṇaiḥ sahitā rājā vedavedāṃgapāragaiḥ |
sarvatra śakrapūjāsu yajñesu parikīrtitaḥ || 41 ||
4.d:
ब्राह्मणैः सहिता राजा वेदवेदांगपारगैः ।
सर्वत्र शक्रपूजासु यज्ञेसु परिकीर्तितः ॥ 41 ॥
4.m: The king, accompanied by brāhmaṇas who have mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, / is proclaimed in all things regarding the worship and sacrifices of Śakra.

4.s: trātāramiti mantro'yaṃ vāsavasya priyaḥ paraḥ |
4.d: त्रातारमिति मन्त्रोऽयं वासवस्य प्रियः परः ।
4.m: The mantra beginning with 'Trātāram' is most dear to Vāsava.

4.s: evaṃ kṛtvā divābhāge śakrotthāpanamāditaḥ || 42 ||
4.d: एवं कृत्वा दिवाभागे शक्रोत्थापनमादितः ॥ 42 ॥
4.m: Having thus performed the raising of Śakra during the daytime initially,

4.s:
śravaṇarkṣayutāyāṃ tu dvādaśyāṃ pārthivaḥ svayam |
antyapāde bharaṇyāṃ tu niśi śakraṃ visarjayet || 43 ||
4.d:
श्रवणर्क्षयुतायां तु द्वादश्यां पार्थिवः स्वयम् ।
अन्त्यपादे भरण्यां तु निशि शक्रं विसर्जयेत् ॥ 43 ॥
4.m: on the twelfth day conjoined with the asterism Śravaṇā, the king himself / should dismiss Śakra at night during the final quarter of Bharaṇī,

4.s:
supteṣu sarvalokeṣu yathā rājā na paśyati |
ṣaṇmāsānmṛtyumāpnoti rājā dṛṣṭvā visarjanam || 44 ||
4.d:
सुप्तेषु सर्वलोकेषु यथा राजा न पश्यति ।
षण्मासान्मृत्युमाप्नोति राजा दृष्ट्वा विसर्जनम् ॥ 44 ॥
4.m: when all people are asleep, in such a way that the king does not see [it]. / If the king sees the dismissal, he incurs death within six months,

4.s:
śakrasya nṛpaśārdūla tasmānnekṣeta tannapaḥ |
visarjanasya mantro'yaṃ purāvidbhirudīritaḥ || 45 ||
4.d:
शक्रस्य नृपशार्दूल तस्मान्नेक्षेत तन्नपः ।
विसर्जनस्य मन्त्रोऽयं पुराविद्भिरुदीरितः ॥ 45 ॥
4.m: O tiger among kings, on account of Śakra; therefore, the king must not look at it. / This mantra for the dismissal has been uttered by knowers of ancient lore:

4.s:
sārdhaṃ surāsuragaṇaiḥ purandara śatakrato |
upahāraṃ gṛhītvema mahendradhvaja gamyatām || 46 ||
4.d:
सार्धं सुरासुरगणैः पुरन्दर शतक्रतो ।
उपहारं गृहीत्वेम महेन्द्रध्वज गम्यताम् ॥ 46 ॥
4.m: 'Together with the hosts of gods and asuras, O Purandara, O Śatakratu, / accepting this offering, depart, O banner of Mahendra!'

4.s:
sūtake tu samutpanne vāre bhaumasya vā śanaiḥ |
bhūmikampādikotpāte vāsavaṃ na visarjayet || 47 ||
4.d:
सूतके तु समुत्पन्ने वारे भौमस्य वा शनैः ।
भूमिकम्पादिकोत्पाते वासवं न विसर्जयेत् ॥ 47 ॥
4.m: If ritual impurity of birth has arisen, or on a Tuesday or a Saturday, / or when an earthquake or similar portent occurs, he should not dismiss Vāsava.

4.s:
utpāte saptarātraṃ tu tathopaplavadarśane |
vyatītya śanibhaumau ca hyanyarkṣe'pi visarjayet || 48 ||
4.d:
उत्पाते सप्तरात्रं तु तथोपप्लवदर्शने ।
व्यतीत्य शनिभौमौ च ह्यन्यर्क्षेऽपि विसर्जयेत् ॥ 48 ॥
4.m: In the case of a portent, for seven nights, or likewise upon seeing a calamity; / passing over Saturday and Tuesday, he should dismiss [him] even under another asterism.

4.s:
sūtake tvatha saṃprāpte vyatīte sūtake punaḥ |
yasmin tasmin dne caiva sūtakānte visarjayet || 49 ||
4.d:
सूतके त्वथ संप्राप्ते व्यतीते सूतके पुनः ।
यस्मिन् तस्मिन् द्ने चैव सूतकान्ते विसर्जयेत् ॥ 49 ॥
4.m: When birth-impurity occurs, after the birth-impurity has passed, / on whatever day it may be at the end of the birth-impurity, he should dismiss [the banner].

4.s:
tathā ketuṃ nṛpo rakṣet patanti śakunā yathā |
na ketau nṛpaśārdūla yāvannahi visarjanam || 50 ||
4.d:
तथा केतुं नृपो रक्षेत् पतन्ति शकुना यथा ।
न केतौ नृपशार्दूल यावन्नहि विसर्जनम् ॥ 50 ॥
4.m: Likewise, the king should guard the banner, so that birds do not alight / upon the banner, O tiger among kings, until the dismissal.

4.s:
śanaiḥ śanaiḥ pātayet tu yathotthāpanamāditaḥ |
kṛtaṃ tathā yathā bhagne ketau mṛtyumavāpnuyāt || 51 ||
4.d:
शनैः शनैः पातयेत् तु यथोत्थापनमादितः ।
कृतं तथा यथा भग्ने केतौ मृत्युमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 51 ॥
4.m: He should lower it very slowly, in the same manner as its raising / was originally done; if the banner is broken, he would meet with death.

4.s:
visṛṣṭaṃ śakraketuṃ tu sālaṅkāraṃ tathā niśi |
kṣipedanena mantreṇa tvagādhe salile nṛpa || 52 ||
4.d:
विसृष्टं शक्रकेतुं तु सालङ्कारं तथा निशि ।
क्षिपेदनेन मन्त्रेण त्वगाधे सलिले नृप ॥ 52 ॥
4.m: At night, with its ornaments, he should cast the dismissed banner of Indra / into deep water, O king, with this mantra:

4.s:
tiṣṭha keto mahābhāga yāvat saṃvatsaraṃ jale |
bhavāya sarvalokānāmantarāya vināśaka || 53 ||
4.d:
तिष्ठ केतो महाभाग यावत् संवत्सरं जले ।
भवाय सर्वलोकानामन्तराय विनाशक ॥ 53 ॥
4.m: “Remain in the water for a year, O illustrious banner, / for the prosperity of all the worlds, O destroyer of obstacles!”

4.s:
utthapayet tūryaravaiḥ sarvalokasya vai puraḥ |
raho visarjayet ketuṃ viśeṣo yaḥ prapūjane || 54 ||
4.d:
उत्थपयेत् तूर्यरवैः सर्वलोकस्य वै पुरः ।
रहो विसर्जयेत् केतुं विशेषो यः प्रपूजने ॥ 54 ॥
4.m: One should raise it with the sounds of musical instruments before all the people; / in secret one should dismiss the banner—such is the distinction in its worship.

4.s:
evaṃ yaḥ kurute pūjāṃ vāsavasya mahātmanaḥ |
sa ciraṃ pṛthivīṃ bhuktvā vāsavaṃ lokamāpnuyāt || 55 ||
4.d:
एवं यः कुरुते पूजां वासवस्य महात्मनः ।
स चिरं पृथिवीं भुक्त्वा वासवं लोकमाप्नुयात् ॥ 55 ॥
4.m: He who thus performs the worship of the magnanimous Vāsava, / having long enjoyed the earth, attains the world of Vāsava.

4.s:
na tasya rājye durbhikṣaṃ nādhayo vyādhayaḥ kvacit |
sthāsyanti mṛtyurnākāle janānāṃ tatra jāyate || 56 ||
4.d:
न तस्य राज्ये दुर्भिक्षं नाधयो व्याधयः क्वचित् ।
स्थास्यन्ति मृत्युर्नाकाले जनानां तत्र जायते ॥ 56 ॥
4.m: In his realm, famine, mental afflictions, and diseases will never / abide anywhere, nor does untimely death befall people there.

4.s:
tattulyaḥ ko'pi nānyo'sti priyaḥ śakrasya pārthiva |
tasya pūjā sarvapūjā keśavādyāśca tatragāḥ || 57 ||
4.d:
तत्तुल्यः कोऽपि नान्योऽस्ति प्रियः शक्रस्य पार्थिव ।
तस्य पूजा सर्वपूजा केशवाद्याश्च तत्रगाः ॥ 57 ॥
4.m: There is no other dear to Indra equal to him, O ruler of the earth; / worship of him is worship of all, and Keśava and the rest are present there.

4.s:
sakalakaluṣahāri vyādhidurbhikṣanāśaṃ
sakalabhavaniveśaṃ sarvasaubhāgyakāri |
surapatigṛhagābhirvārcanaṃ śakraketoḥ
pratiśaradamanekaiḥ pūjayecchrīvivṛddhayai || 58 ||
4.d:
सकलकलुषहारि व्याधिदुर्भिक्षनाशं
सकलभवनिवेशं सर्वसौभाग्यकारि ।
सुरपतिगृहगाभिर्वार्चनं शक्रकेतोः
प्रतिशरदमनेकैः पूजयेच्छ्रीविवृद्धयै ॥ 58 ॥
4.m: Which removes all defilements, destroys disease and famine, / establishes all homes, and produces all good fortune— / the worship of Indra’s banner along with the women of the king of gods’ abode / should be performed every autumn with many [offerings] for the increase of prosperity.

4.s: iti śrīkālikāpurāṇe saptāśītitamo'dhyāyaḥ || 87 ||
4.d: इति श्रीकालिकापुराणे सप्ताशीतितमोऽध्यायः ॥ 87 ॥
4.m: Thus ends the eighty-seventh chapter in the glorious Kālikāpurāṇa.

4.s: aṣṭāśītitamo'dhyāyaḥ
4.d: अष्टाशीतितमोऽध्यायः

4.s: aurva uvāca -
4.d: और्व उवाच -

4.s:
jyeṣṭha daśaharāyāṃ tu viṣṇoriṣṭiṃ nṛpa śṛṇu | yena vā vidhinā
kuryādiṣṭiṃ viṣnornṛpaḥ sadā || 1 ||
4.d:
ज्येष्ठ दशहरायां तु विष्णोरिष्टिं नृप शृणु । येन वा विधिना
कुर्यादिष्टिं विष्नोर्नृपः सदा ॥ 1 ॥
4.m: Hear now, O king, of the sacrifice to Viṣṇu on the Daśaharā of Jyeṣṭha, / by which rite the king should always perform the sacrifice to Viṣṇu.

4.s:
pratyabdaṃ pārthivaḥ kuryāt pratimāṃ kāñcanīṃ hareḥ |
anyatejīmayīṃ vāpi dāravīṃ vā śilāmayīm || 2 ||
4.d:
प्रत्यब्दं पार्थिवः कुर्यात् प्रतिमां काञ्चनीं हरेः ।
अन्यतेजीमयीं वापि दारवीं वा शिलामयीम् ॥ 2 ॥
4.m: Every year the ruler of the earth should make an image of Hari out of gold, / or composed of other metals, or made of wood, or of stone.

4.s:
tāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya vidhinā mānonmānaistu śilpibhiḥ |
pratiṣṭhāṃ vidhivat tasyāḥ kuryād vipraiḥ purohitaiḥ || 3 ||
4.d:
तां प्रतिष्ठाप्य विधिना मानोन्मानैस्तु शिल्पिभिः ।
प्रतिष्ठां विधिवत् तस्याः कुर्याद् विप्रैः पुरोहितैः ॥ 3 ॥
4.m: Having fashioned it according to rule with proportions and measurements by artisans, / he should perform its consecration according to rule through brāhmaṇas and royal priests.

4.s:
tāṃ saṃsthāpya surāgāre svayaṃ vā yatnataḥ kṛte |
vāsudevasya bījena pūrvoktavidhinā tathā || 4 ||
4.d:
तां संस्थाप्य सुरागारे स्वयं वा यत्नतः कृते ।
वासुदेवस्य बीजेन पूर्वोक्तविधिना तथा ॥ 4 ॥
4.m: Having installed it in a temple of the gods or one made by himself with effort, / with the seed-syllable of Vāsudeva according to the previously stated rule,

4.s:
sarvopacārairbhaktyā nu vāsudevaṃ prapūjayet |
pūjānte saṃskṛte vahnau kuṇḍamadhye sthito dvijaḥ || 5 ||
4.d:
सर्वोपचारैर्भक्त्या नु वासुदेवं प्रपूजयेत् ।
पूजान्ते संस्कृते वह्नौ कुण्डमध्ये स्थितो द्विजः ॥ 5 ॥
4.m: he should indeed worship Vāsudeva with devotion with all offerings. / At the end of the worship, standing within the hearth beside the consecrated fire, the twice-born

4.s:
ājyaiḥ sahasraṃ juhuyādāhutīnāṃ hareḥ priyam |
saṃpūjya vāsudevaṃ tu homaṃ kṛtvā tato dvijaḥ || 6 ||
4.d:
आज्यैः सहस्रं जुहुयादाहुतीनां हरेः प्रियम् ।
संपूज्य वासुदेवं तु होमं कृत्वा ततो द्विजः ॥ 6 ॥
4.m: should offer a thousand oblations with clarified butter, dear to Hari. / Having worshipped Vāsudeva and then made the fire-offering, the twice-born,

4.s:
nṛpasyānumate tāṃ tu pratimāṃ maṇḍalaṃ nayet |
pratimāyāḥ kapolau dvau spṛṣṭvā dakṣiṇapāṇinā || 7 ||
4.d:
नृपस्यानुमते तां तु प्रतिमां मण्डलं नयेत् ।
प्रतिमायाः कपोलौ द्वौ स्पृष्ट्वा दक्षिणपाणिना ॥ 7 ॥
4.m: with the king’s permission, should bring that image to the maṇḍala. / Touching the two cheeks of the image with his right hand,

4.s:
prāṇapratiṣṭhāṃ kurvīta tasyāṃ devasya vai hareḥ |
kṛtāyāṃ tu pratiṣṭhāyāṃ prāṇānāṃ nṛpasattama || 8 ||
4.d:
प्राणप्रतिष्ठां कुर्वीत तस्यां देवस्य वै हरेः ।
कृतायां तु प्रतिष्ठायां प्राणानां नृपसत्तम ॥ 8 ॥
4.m: he should perform the installation of the breath of the god Hari in it. / When the installation of the vital breaths has been performed, O best of kings,

4.s:
viṣṇuprāṇāstāṃ pratimāmāyānti niyataṃ svayam |
prāṇeṣvathāgateṣvasyāṃ devatvaṃ niyataṃ bhavet || 9 ||
4.d:
विष्णुप्राणास्तां प्रतिमामायान्ति नियतं स्वयम् ।
प्राणेष्वथागतेष्वस्यां देवत्वं नियतं भवेत् ॥ 9 ॥
4.m: the vital breaths of Viṣṇu certainly come of themselves to that image; / and when the vital breaths have entered into it, divinity certainly arises.

4.s:
akṛtāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāyāṃ prāṇānāṃ pratimāsu ca |
yathāpūrvaṃ tathābhāvaḥ svarṇādīnāṃ na viṣṇutā || 10 ||
4.d:
अकृतायां प्रतिष्ठायां प्राणानां प्रतिमासु च ।
यथापूर्वं तथाभावः स्वर्णादीनां न विष्णुता ॥ 10 ॥
4.m: If the installation of the vital breaths is not performed in the images, / the gold and other materials remain just as before, not the state of being Viṣṇu.

4.s:
anyeṣāmapi devānāṃ pratimāsvapi pārthiva |
prāṇapratiṣṭhā kartavyā tasyā devatvasiddhaye || 11 ||
4.d:
अन्येषामपि देवानां प्रतिमास्वपि पार्थिव ।
प्राणप्रतिष्ठा कर्तव्या तस्या देवत्वसिद्धये ॥ 11 ॥
4.m: In the images of other gods as well, O ruler of the earth, / the installation of the vital breaths must be performed for the accomplishment of their divinity.

4.s:
suvarṇaṃ tu suvarṇaṃ syācchilā dāru tathā śilā |
anyacca svasvarūpaṃ syāt prāṇasthānamṛte sadā || 12 ||
4.d:
सुवर्णं तु सुवर्णं स्याच्छिला दारु तथा शिला ।
अन्यच्च स्वस्वरूपं स्यात् प्राणस्थानमृते सदा ॥ 12 ॥
4.m: Gold would just be gold, stone [and] wood [would just be] stone, / and other things would remain in their own nature, always without the abode of the vital breaths.

4.s:
vāsudevasya bījena tad viṣṇorityanena ca |
tathaivāṅgāṅgimantrābhyāṃ pratiṣṭhāmācareddhareḥ || 13 ||
4.d:
वासुदेवस्य बीजेन तद् विष्णोरित्यनेन च ।
तथैवाङ्गाङ्गिमन्त्राभ्यां प्रतिष्ठामाचरेद्धरेः ॥ 13 ॥
4.m: With the seed-syllable of Vāsudeva and with [the verse] "tad viṣṇoḥ [paramam padam]", / and likewise with the limb-mantras and the primary mantra, he should perform the consecration of Hari.

4.s:
tathaiva hṛdaye'ṅguṣṭhaṃ dattvā śaśvacca mantravit |
ebhirmantraiḥ pratiṣṭhāpya hṛdaye'pi samācaret || 14 ||
4.d:
तथैव हृदयेऽङ्गुष्ठं दत्त्वा शश्वच्च मन्त्रवित् ।
एभिर्मन्त्रैः प्रतिष्ठाप्य हृदयेऽपि समाचरेत् ॥ 14 ॥
4.m: Likewise, placing his thumb on the heart, continuously, the knower of mantras, / having established [the deity] with these mantras, should also perform it upon the heart:

4.s:
asyai prāṇāḥ pratiṣṭhantu asyai prāṇāḥ kṣarantu yat |
asau devatvasaṃkhyāyai svāheti yajuruccaran || 15 ||
4.d:
अस्यै प्राणाः प्रतिष्ठन्तु अस्यै प्राणाः क्षरन्तु यत् ।
असौ देवत्वसंख्यायै स्वाहेति यजुरुच्चरन् ॥ 15 ॥
4.m: “May the vital breaths be established in this; may the vital breaths stream into this, / so that this may be reckoned as divinity, svāhā!”—uttering this yajus-mantra,

4.s:
aṅgamantrairaṅgimantrairvaidikairityanena ca |
prāṇapratiṣṭhāṃ sarvatra pratimāsu samācaret || 16 ||
4.d:
अङ्गमन्त्रैरङ्गिमन्त्रैर्वैदिकैरित्यनेन च ।
प्राणप्रतिष्ठां सर्वत्र प्रतिमासु समाचरेत् ॥ 16 ॥
4.m: and with the limb-mantras, the primary mantras, and the Vedic mantras, / he should everywhere perform the installation of the vital breaths in images.

4.s:
pratimāpūjane kuryādātmanyapi ca mantravit |
prāṇapratiṣṭhāṃ prathamaṃ pūjābhāgaviśuddhaye || 17 ||
4.d:
प्रतिमापूजने कुर्यादात्मन्यपि च मन्त्रवित् ।
प्राणप्रतिष्ठां प्रथमं पूजाभागविशुद्धये ॥ 17 ॥
4.m: In the worship of an image, the knower of mantras should first perform / the installation of the vital breaths in himself as well, for the purification of his share in the worship.

4.s:
asmin prāṇapratiṣṭhāṃ tu pratimāpūjanādṛte |
na kaścit tu budhaḥ kuryāt kṛtvā mṛtyumavāpnuyāt || 18 ||
4.d:
अस्मिन् प्राणप्रतिष्ठां तु प्रतिमापूजनादृते ।
न कश्चित् तु बुधः कुर्यात् कृत्वा मृत्युमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 18 ॥
4.m: Except in the worship of an image, no wise person / should perform the installation of the vital breaths in this [body]; having done so, he would meet with death.

4.s:
viṣṇoriṣṭimimāṃ kṛtvā daśamyāṃ pārthivottamaḥ |
tasyāmeva tu pūrṇāyāṃ pratimāṃ sthāpayet tataḥ || 19 ||
4.d:
विष्णोरिष्टिमिमां कृत्वा दशम्यां पार्थिवोत्तमः ।
तस्यामेव तु पूर्णायां प्रतिमां स्थापयेत् ततः ॥ 19 ॥
4.m: Having performed this sacrifice to Viṣṇu on the tenth [day], the best of rulers of the earth / should then install the image on that very full [day].

4.s:
evaṃ daśaharāyāṃ tu kṛtveṣṭiṃ pārthivo hareḥ |
sarvān kāmānavāpnoti nirvighno'pi sa jāyate || 20 ||
4.d:
एवं दशहरायां तु कृत्वेष्टिं पार्थिवो हरेः ।
सर्वान् कामानवाप्नोति निर्विघ्नोऽपि स जायते ॥ 20 ॥
4.m: Having thus performed the sacrifice to Hari on Daśaharā, the ruler of the earth / attains all desires, and he becomes free from obstacles.

4.s:
śrīpaṃcamyāṃ śriyaṃ devīṃ kundaiḥ saṃpūjayetsadā |
vāsavaṃ gajarājasthamupahāraistathottamaiḥ || 21 ||
4.d:
श्रीपंचम्यां श्रियं देवीं कुन्दैः संपूजयेत्सदा ।
वासवं गजराजस्थमुपहारैस्तथोत्तमैः ॥ 21 ॥
4.m: On Śrīpañcamī he should always worship the goddess Śrī with jasmine flowers, / and Vāsava mounted on the king of elephants with excellent offerings.

4.s:
lakṣmyāstantraṃ mahāmantraṃ vāsavasya puroditam |
atrāpi pūjane grāhyaṃ maṇḍalādi yathākramam || 22 ||
4.d:
लक्ष्म्यास्तन्त्रं महामन्त्रं वासवस्य पुरोदितम् ।
अत्रापि पूजने ग्राह्यं मण्डलादि यथाक्रमम् ॥ 22 ॥
4.m: The tantra of Lakṣmī and the great mantra of Vāsava were stated earlier; / here too, in worship, they are to be adopted along with the maṇḍala and so forth in due order.

4.s:
evaṃ kṛte pūjane tu śrīpaṃcamyāṃ viśeṣataḥ |
śrīyuto nṛpatirbhūyānna śrīhānimavāpnuyāt || 23 ||
4.d:
एवं कृते पूजने तु श्रीपंचम्यां विशेषतः ।
श्रीयुतो नृपतिर्भूयान्न श्रीहानिमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 23 ॥
4.m: When worship is thus performed, especially on Śrīpañcamī, / the king becomes endowed with prosperity and does not suffer the loss of prosperity.

4.s:
sadācāraviśeṣo'yaṃ kathitastava pārthiva |
niṣedhe tu viśeṣāṃśca śṛṇu yena śriyeṣyate || 24 ||
4.d:
सदाचारविशेषोऽयं कथितस्तव पार्थिव ।
निषेधे तु विशेषांश्च शृणु येन श्रियेष्यते ॥ 24 ॥
4.m: This particular good conduct has been declared to you, O ruler of the earth; / hear also the particulars among prohibitions, by which prosperity is desired:

4.s:
asaṃpūjya tathā viṣṇuṁ śivamagniṃ purandaram |
adattvā ca tathā dānaṃ na bhuñjīta nṛpaḥ kvacit || 25 ||
4.d:
असंपूज्य तथा विष्णुṁ शिवमग्निं पुरन्दरम् ।
अदत्त्वा च तथा दानं न भुञ्जीत नृपः क्वचित् ॥ 25 ॥
4.m: Without having worshipped Viṣṇu, Śiva, Agni, and Purandara, / and without having given gifts, the king should never eat anywhere.

4.s:
hāvayedagnihotraṃ tu nityameva purohitaiḥ |
akṛtvā cāgnihotraṃ tu bhuñjannarakamāpnuyāt || 26 ||
4.d:
हावयेदग्निहोत्रं तु नित्यमेव पुरोहितैः ।
अकृत्वा चाग्निहोत्रं तु भुञ्जन्नरकमाप्नुयात् ॥ 26 ॥
4.m: He should have the agnihotra offered constantly by royal priests; / eating without having performed the agnihotra, he would go to hell.

4.s:
nārakṣite gṛhe rājā ratnadīpavivarjite |
svapet tathā striyā sārdhaṃ na kadācana saṃviśet || 20 ||
4.d:
नारक्षिते गृहे राजा रत्नदीपविवर्जिते ।
स्वपेत् तथा स्त्रिया सार्धं न कदाचन संविशेत् ॥ 20 ॥
4.m: In an unguarded room, devoid of jewel-lamps, the king / should not sleep, nor should he ever lie down with a woman [there].

4.s:
bhuktvānnaṃ śrīphalaṃ nādyāt tathā dhātrīphalaṃ nṛpaḥ |
buddhikṣayakarā hyetā māṣa āsavamṛttikāḥ || 28 ||
4.d:
भुक्त्वान्नं श्रीफलं नाद्यात् तथा धात्रीफलं नृपः ।
बुद्धिक्षयकरा ह्येता माष आसवमृत्तिकाः ॥ 28 ॥
4.m: Having eaten food, the king should not eat wood-apple or emblic myrobalan; / for these cause the decay of intellect: black gram, fermented liquor, and clay.

4.s:
nimbāṭarūṣacyutāśca buddhivṛddhikarā matāḥ |
buddhikṣayakarān nityaṃ tvajedrājā ca bhojane || 29 ||
4.d:
निम्बाटरूषच्युताश्च बुद्धिवृद्धिकरा मताः ।
बुद्धिक्षयकरान् नित्यं त्वजेद्राजा च भोजने ॥ 29 ॥
4.m: Leaves fallen from neem and aṭarūṣa are considered enhancers of intellect; / the king should always avoid in his food those things that cause the decay of intellect.

4.s:
bhakṣayedanvahaṃ buddhivṛddhihetuṃ nṛpottamaḥ |
na paryāyavihīnaṃ tu prārohedāsanaṃ nṛpaḥ || 30 ||
4.d:
भक्षयेदन्वहं बुद्धिवृद्धिहेतुं नृपोत्तमः ।
न पर्यायविहीनं तु प्रारोहेदासनं नृपः ॥ 30 ॥
4.m: The best of kings should daily eat what causes the increase of intellect. / A king should not mount a seat that is out of order,

4.s:
na yānaṃ na gajaṃ nāśvamāroheddhīnamāsanaiḥ |
naikastu vicaredrājā kadācidapi nirjane || 31 ||
4.d:
न यानं न गजं नाश्वमारोहेद्धीनमासनैः ।
नैकस्तु विचरेद्राजा कदाचिदपि निर्जने ॥ 31 ॥
4.m: nor mount a carriage, an elephant, or a horse lacking seats. / The king should never wander alone in a solitary place.

4.s:
madahetuṃ na bhuṃjīyāt kadācidapi bhojane |
kadācinnāpi seveta hyaṣṭamyāṃ māṃsamaithune || 32 ||
4.d:
मदहेतुं न भुंजीयात् कदाचिदपि भोजने ।
कदाचिन्नापि सेवेत ह्यष्टम्यां मांसमैथुने ॥ 32 ॥
4.m: He should never eat anything that causes intoxication in his meal; / he should never indulge in meat or sexual intercourse on the eighth [lunar day].

4.s:
darśaśrāddhaṃ gayāśrāddhaṃ tilaistarpaṇameva ca |
na jīvatpitṛko bhūpa kuryāt kṛtvāghamāpnuyāt || 33 ||
4.d:
दर्शश्राद्धं गयाश्राद्धं तिलैस्तर्पणमेव च ।
न जीवत्पितृको भूप कुर्यात् कृत्वाघमाप्नुयात् ॥ 33 ॥
4.m: The new-moon śrāddha, the Gayā-śrāddha, and the water-libation with sesame seeds— / one whose father is living, O king, should not perform; having performed [them], he incurs sin.

4.s:
na kṣetrajādīṃstanayān rājye rājābhiṣecayet |
pitṛṇāṃ śūddhaye nityamaurase tanaye sati || 34 ||
4.d:
न क्षेत्रजादींस्तनयान् राज्ये राजाभिषेचयेत् ।
पितृणां शूद्धये नित्यमौरसे तनये सति ॥ 34 ॥
4.m: A king should not consecrate sons such as the kṣetraja for sovereignty / when there is a legitimate son (aurasa), for the constant purification of the ancestors.

4.s:
aurasaḥ kṣetrajaścaiva dattaḥ kṛtrima eva ca |
gūḍhotpanno'paviddhaśca bhāgārhāstanayā ime || 35 ||
4.d:
औरसः क्षेत्रजश्चैव दत्तः कृत्रिम एव च ।
गूढोत्पन्नोऽपविद्धश्च भागार्हास्तनया इमे ॥ 35 ॥
4.m: The legitimate son (aurasa), the wife's son (kṣetraja), the adopted son (datta), the made son (kṛtrima), / the secretly born (gūḍhotpanna), and the abandoned (apaviddha)—these sons are entitled to a share.

4.s:
kāttīnaśca sahoḍhaśca krītaḥ paunarbhavastathā |
svayaṃdattaśca dāsaśca ṣaḍate putrapāṃsulāḥ || 36 ||
4.d:
कात्तीनश्च सहोढश्च क्रीतः पौनर्भवस्तथा ।
स्वयंदत्तश्च दासश्च षडते पुत्रपांसुलाः ॥ 36 ॥
